title.raw: 卷41 源賀 Volume 41: Yuan He

sentences.zh: 源賀，自署河西王禿髮傉檀之子也。

translations.literal: Yuan He was the son of Tufa Rutan, who had styled himself King of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan He was a son of Tufa Rutan, who had proclaimed himself King of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 傉檀為乞伏熾磐所滅，賀自樂都來奔。

translations.literal: When Rutan was destroyed by Qifu Chipan, He came from Ledu to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: After Rutan was overthrown by Qifu Chipan, He fled from Ledu to offer his allegiance.

sentences.zh: 賀偉容貌，善風儀。

translations.literal: He was imposing in appearance and skilled in bearing and deportment.
translations.idiomatic: He was a man of striking looks and dignified presence.

sentences.zh: 世祖素聞其名，及見，器其機辯，賜爵西平侯，加龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu had long heard his name; when they met, he valued his quick wit, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Xiping, and added the title General Who Gallops Like a Dragon.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu had heard of him long before; at their first meeting he was impressed by his sharp mind, made him Marquis of Xiping, and appointed him General Who Gallops Like a Dragon.

sentences.zh: 謂賀曰：「卿與朕源同，因事分姓，今可為源氏。」

translations.literal: He said to He: "You and I share the same origin; because of events our surnames were divided. From now on you may take the surname Yuan."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him, "You and I spring from the same source; circumstances split our clans, but from now on you shall bear the surname Yuan."

sentences.zh: 從擊叛胡白龍，又討吐京胡，皆先登陷陳。

translations.literal: He followed in campaigns against the rebel Hu Bai Long and also attacked the Tujing Hu, in every case being first to scale and break the enemy lines.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the suppression of the rebel Bai Long and in campaigns against the Tujing Hu, always among the first to storm the enemy ranks.

sentences.zh: 進號平西將軍。

translations.literal: He was advanced to the title General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 世祖征涼州，以賀為鄉導。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu campaigned against Liangzhou, he made He his guide.
translations.idiomatic: On Emperor Taiwu's Liangzhou campaign, He served as pathfinder.

sentences.zh: 詔問攻戰之計，賀對曰：「姑臧城外有四部鮮卑，各為之援。

translations.literal: The emperor inquired about plans for attack; He replied: "Outside Guzang city four Xianbei divisions each serve as its allies.
translations.idiomatic: Asked for a battle plan, He said, "Four Xianbei divisions outside Guzang each supply the city with support.

sentences.zh: 然皆是臣祖父舊民，臣願軍前宣國威信，示其福禍，必相率歸降。

translations.literal: Yet they are all former subjects of my grandfather; I wish to go before the army and proclaim the state's authority, showing them fortune and disaster—they will surely submit in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they were all once my grandfather's people. Let me go ahead of the army and proclaim the empire's authority, showing them what they stand to gain or lose—they will surely come over in droves.

sentences.zh: 外援既服，然後攻其孤城，拔之如反掌耳。」

translations.literal: Once the external allies have submitted, then attack the isolated city—taking it will be like turning one's palm."
translations.idiomatic: Once their outside support is won over, you can strike the isolated city and take it as easily as turning your hand."

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「善。」

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu said, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 於是遣賀率精騎歷諸部招慰，下三萬餘落，獲雜畜十餘萬頭。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent He at the head of elite cavalry to visit the various divisions and win them over; more than thirty thousand households submitted, and over a hundred thousand head of mixed livestock were taken.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent He with picked cavalry to tour the tribes and win them over. More than thirty thousand households came in, and over a hundred thousand head of livestock were gathered.

sentences.zh: 及圍姑臧，由是無外慮，故得專力攻之。

translations.literal: When they besieged Guzang, there was thus no worry from outside, and they could concentrate their strength on the assault.
translations.idiomatic: When the siege of Guzang began, there was no longer any threat from outside, so the army could throw its full weight against the city.

sentences.zh: 涼州平，遷征西將軍，進號西平公。

translations.literal: When Liangzhou was pacified, he was transferred to General Who Campaigns West and advanced to Duke of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: After Liangzhou was pacified, he was made General Who Campaigns West and promoted to Duke of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 又從征蠕蠕，擊五城、吐京胡，討蓋吳諸賊，皆有功。

translations.literal: He again followed campaigns against the Rouran, struck Wucheng and the Tujing Hu, and suppressed the bandits led by Gai Wu—all with merit.
translations.idiomatic: He also joined campaigns against the Rouran, fought at Wucheng and against the Tujing Hu, and helped put down Gai Wu and other rebels, distinguishing himself in each.

sentences.zh: 拜散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Regular Attendant at the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed regular attendant at the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 從駕臨江，為前鋒大將。

translations.literal: He accompanied the emperor to the Yangzi and served as commander of the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor on the Yangzi campaign as commander of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 賀為人雄果，每遇強寇，輒自奮擊。

translations.literal: He was by nature bold and resolute; whenever he met fierce enemies he would charge forward himself.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was bold and fierce; whenever he met a strong foe he would throw himself into the fight.

sentences.zh: 世祖戒之曰：「兵凶戰危，不宜輕犯，卿可運籌處分，勿恃身力也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu admonished him: "War is inauspicious and battle perilous—you should not lightly expose yourself. You should plan and command; do not rely on personal strength."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu warned him, "War is cruel and battle dangerous—you must not rush in so lightly. Leave the planning to your staff and do not stake everything on your own arm."

sentences.zh: 賀本名破羌，是役也，世祖曰：「人之立名，宜其得實，[1]何可濫也。」

translations.literal: His original name was Poqiang. In this campaign Emperor Taiwu said: "When a man receives a name it should match the truth;[1] how can it be applied loosely?"
translations.idiomatic: He's original name had been Poqiang, "Smash the Qiang." After this campaign Emperor Taiwu said, "A man's name ought to fit what he truly is;[1] it must not be given lightly."

sentences.zh: 賜名賀焉。

translations.literal: He was granted the name He.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the name He, "Celebrate."

sentences.zh: 拜殿中尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed director of the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 南安王余為宗愛所殺也，賀部勒禁兵，靜遏外內，與南部尚書陸麗決議定策，翼戴高宗。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Nan'an, Yu, was killed by Zong'ai, He mustered the palace guard, calmed inside and out, and with Lu Li, Director of the Southern Department, settled on a plan to support and install Emperor Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Prince of Nan'an Yu was murdered by Zong'ai, He rallied the palace guard, kept order within and without, and with Lu Li of the southern secretariat devised the plan to place Emperor Wencheng on the throne.

sentences.zh: 令麗與劉尼馳詣苑中，奉迎高宗，賀守禁中為之內應。

translations.literal: He ordered Li and Liu Ni to gallop to the park to welcome Emperor Wencheng, while He held the palace interior as inner support.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Li and Liu Ni at full speed to the imperial park to bring back Emperor Wencheng, while he held the palace gates as their contact within.

sentences.zh: 俄而麗抱高宗單騎而至，賀乃開門。

translations.literal: Before long Li arrived carrying Emperor Wencheng on a single horse, and He opened the gates.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Li arrived with the young emperor in his arms, riding alone, and He threw open the gates.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，社稷大安，賀有力焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wencheng took the throne the altars of state were greatly secured—He had force in this.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wencheng ascended the throne the realm was secured, and He had done much to make it so.

sentences.zh: 轉征北將軍，加給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Campaigns North and added as Supervising Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to general who campaigns north and made supervising attendant.

sentences.zh: 以定策之勳，進爵西平王。

translations.literal: For merit in settling the succession he was advanced to Prince of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: For his role in securing the succession he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，班賜百僚，謂賀曰：「朕大賚善人，卿其任意取之，勿謙退也。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Wencheng took the throne he distributed largess to the hundred officials and said to He: "I greatly reward good men—take what you will, do not decline out of modesty."
translations.idiomatic: At his accession the emperor distributed rewards to the court and told He, "I mean to reward the worthy handsomely—take whatever you like and do not hold back out of modesty."

sentences.zh: 賀辭，固使取之，賀唯取戎馬一匹而已。

translations.literal: He declined; the emperor pressed him to take, and He took only a single warhorse.
translations.idiomatic: He demurred; when the emperor insisted, he accepted only one warhorse.

sentences.zh: 是時，斷獄多濫，賀上書曰：「案律：謀反之家，其子孫雖養他族，追還就戮，所以絕罪人之類，彰大逆之辜；

translations.literal: At that time criminal judgments were often excessive. He memorialized: "According to the statutes, in families guilty of treason the sons and grandsons, though raised in other clans, are pursued and executed—thus to cut off the line of criminals and make manifest the crime of great rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: Judicial punishments were then often excessive. He submitted a memorial: "The law provides that in cases of treason, even sons and grandsons raised in other households are hunted down and executed, so that the line of the guilty may be cut off and the gravity of rebellion made plain;

sentences.zh: 其為劫賊應誅者，兄弟子姪在遠，道隔關津，皆不坐。

translations.literal: for robbery deserving death, brothers, sons, and nephews who are far away with roads and passes between are not punished.
translations.idiomatic: yet for robbery warranting death, brothers, sons, and nephews living far away beyond passes and barriers are not punished.

sentences.zh: 竊惟先朝制律之意，以不同謀，非絕類之罪，故特垂不死之詔。

translations.literal: I reflect that the intent of the former court in making the law was that not sharing in the plot is not a crime of extinction, and therefore they specially granted the edict of non-execution.
translations.idiomatic: I take it that the intent of the previous reign in framing the law was that those who did not share in the plot should not suffer extinction, and therefore issued the special edict sparing their lives.

sentences.zh: 若年十三已下，家人首惡，計謀所不及，愚以為可原其命，沒入縣官。」

translations.literal: If below thirteen years of age, though of the household of the chief culprit, beyond the reach of plotting—I humbly think their lives may be spared and they be enrolled as government slaves."
translations.idiomatic: Children thirteen and under, though of the chief culprit's household, cannot have shared in the design. I humbly propose that their lives be spared and they be enrolled as government dependents."

sentences.zh: 高宗納之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wencheng adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wencheng accepted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 出為征南將軍、冀州刺史，改封隴西王，賀上書曰：「臣聞：人之所寶，莫寶於生全；

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Campaigns South and Inspector of Jizhou, was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Longxi, and memorialized: "Your servant has heard: what men treasure, nothing is treasured like preserving life;
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as general who campaigns south and inspector of Jizhou, and was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Longxi. He wrote: "I have heard that among all things men prize, none is prized like life itself;

sentences.zh: 德之厚者，莫厚於宥死。

translations.literal: among thick virtues, none is thicker than sparing death.
translations.idiomatic: and among the deepest acts of virtue, none is deeper than sparing the condemned.

sentences.zh: 然犯死之罪，難以盡恕，權其輕重，有可矜恤。

translations.literal: Yet crimes deserving death are hard to pardon entirely; weighing light and heavy, there are cases deserving compassion.
translations.idiomatic: Yet crimes warranting death cannot all be forgiven outright; still, when their gravity is weighed, some deserve compassion.

sentences.zh: 今勁寇遊魂於北，狡賊負險於南，其在疆埸，猶須防戍。

translations.literal: Now fierce enemies roam the north and cunning bandits hold perilous ground in the south; on the borders defense is still needed.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful foes still haunt the north and crafty rebels hold the south's defiles; the frontiers still need garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為自非大逆、赤手殺人之罪，其坐贓及盜與過誤之愆應入死者，皆可原命，謫守邊境。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly thinks that apart from great rebellion and murder with bare hands, those guilty of corruption, theft, and negligent faults who should enter death may all have life spared and be banished to guard the borders.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly propose that except for treason and murder with one's own hand, all who would die for corruption, theft, or lesser faults may be spared and sent to serve on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 是則已斷之體，更受全生之恩；

translations.literal: Thus those whose bodies were already forfeit would again receive the grace of full life;
translations.idiomatic: Men already condemned to die would receive the gift of life anew;

sentences.zh: 徭役之家，漸蒙休息之惠。

translations.literal: households of corvée labor would gradually receive the benefit of rest.
translations.idiomatic: and households burdened with corvée would gradually know relief.

sentences.zh: 刑措之化，庶幾在茲。

translations.literal: The transformation of punishments set aside would perhaps lie herein.
translations.idiomatic: The age when punishments need seldom be used might draw near.

sentences.zh: 虞書曰『流宥五刑』，此其義也。

translations.literal: The Book of Yu says 'banishment and pardon for the five punishments'—this is the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Yu speaks of banishment and pardon in place of the five punishments—this is that very principle.

sentences.zh: 臣受恩深重，無以仰答，將違闕庭，豫增係戀，敢上瞽言，唯加裁察。」

translations.literal: Your servant has received deep grace and has no means to repay it upward; about to leave the court I beforehand increase my attachment, and dare offer blind words—may you add judgment and inspection."
translations.idiomatic: I have received such deep favor that I cannot repay it; as I am soon to leave the capital my attachment only grows. I venture this humble counsel and beg your judgment."

sentences.zh: 高宗納之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wencheng adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wencheng accepted it.

sentences.zh: 已後入死者，皆恕死徙邊。

translations.literal: Afterward all who would have entered death were pardoned from death and moved to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter all who would have been executed were spared and sent to the border garrisons.

sentences.zh: 久之，高宗謂羣臣曰：「源賀勸朕宥諸死刑，徙充北番諸戍，自爾至今，一歲所活殊為不少，生濟之理既多，邊戍之兵有益。

translations.literal: After some time Emperor Wencheng told the assembled ministers: "Yuan He urged me to pardon all capital sentences and move them to fill the northern garrisons; from then until now, in a year those kept alive are quite numerous—the principle of sustaining life has much increased, and the border garrisons have benefited.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later Emperor Wencheng told the court, "Yuan He persuaded me to spare those condemned to death and send them to the northern posts. In the year since, the number of lives saved has been considerable, many more people have been given a chance to live, and the frontier garrisons have gained useful men.

sentences.zh: 卿等事朕，致何善意也？

translations.literal: You who serve me—what good intent have you shown?
translations.idiomatic: You who serve me—what comparable good have you done for me?

sentences.zh: 苟人人如賀，朕治天下復何憂哉！

translations.literal: If every man were like He, what worry would I have in governing the realm!
translations.idiomatic: If every one of you were like He, what would I have left to worry about in ruling the realm!

sentences.zh: 顧憶誠言，[2]利實廣矣。」

translations.literal: Looking back on his sincere words,[2] the benefit is truly broad."
translations.idiomatic: When I think back on his honest counsel,[2] the good it has done is immense."

sentences.zh: 羣臣咸曰：「非忠臣不能進此計，非聖明不能納此言。」

translations.literal: The assembled ministers all said: "Only a loyal minister could advance this plan; only a sage ruler could adopt these words."
translations.idiomatic: The ministers all replied, "Only a loyal minister could propose such a measure, and only a sage ruler could accept it."

sentences.zh: 賀之臨州，鞫獄以情，徭役簡省。

translations.literal: When He came to his province he judged cases according to the facts and simplified corvée labor.
translations.idiomatic: In his province He tried cases on their merits and lightened corvée burdens.

sentences.zh: 武邑郡姦人石華告沙門道可與賀謀反，有司以聞。

translations.literal: The villain Shi Hua of Wuyi commandery reported that the monk Daoke was plotting rebellion with He; the authorities reported it.
translations.idiomatic: A local scoundrel named Shi Hua in Wuyi commandery accused the monk Daoke of plotting rebellion with He, and the matter was reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 高宗謂羣臣曰：「賀誠心事國，朕為卿等保之，無此明矣。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wencheng told the ministers: "He serves the state with sincere heart—I vouch for him before you; this is not clear."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wencheng told the court, "He serves the state with utter loyalty. I stake my word on him before you all—this charge is plainly false."

sentences.zh: 乃精加訊檢，華果引誣。

translations.literal: He then conducted a thorough interrogation, and Hua indeed confessed to false accusation.
translations.idiomatic: A careful investigation followed, and Hua confessed to fabricating the charge.

sentences.zh: 於是遣使者詔賀曰：「卿以忠誠款至，著自先朝，以丹青之潔而受蒼蠅之汙。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent an envoy with an edict to He: "You have been loyal and sincere in utmost degree, renowned since the former court, yet like vermilion purity you have suffered the stain of flies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent an envoy with an edict: "Your loyalty has been beyond question since the previous reign, yet like pure vermilion you have been smeared by flies.

sentences.zh: 朕登時研檢，已加極法，故遣宣意。

translations.literal: I immediately investigated and have already applied the extreme penalty—therefore I send this to declare my intent.
translations.idiomatic: I looked into the matter at once and have already punished the accuser to the full extent of the law. I send this word so you will know my mind.

sentences.zh: 其善綏所莅，勿以囂謗之言致損慮也。」

translations.literal: Continue to govern well where you are posted; do not let clamorous slander harm your peace of mind."
translations.idiomatic: Continue to govern your province well, and do not let malicious gossip trouble you."

sentences.zh: 賀上書謝，書奏，高宗顧謂左右曰：「以賀之忠誠，尚致其誣，不若是者，可無慎乎！」

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial of thanks; when the memorial was presented Emperor Wencheng turned to those beside him and said: "With He's loyalty he still met false accusation—if not such as he, need one not be cautious!"
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a letter of thanks. When it was read, Emperor Wencheng turned to his attendants and said, "If even a man as loyal as He can be slandered, how much more must lesser men watch their step!"

sentences.zh: 時考殿最，賀治為第一，賜衣馬器物，班宣天下。

translations.literal: At the time of assessing excellence in office, He's governance ranked first; he was given robes, horses, and objects, and this was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the annual review of officials his administration ranked first. He was rewarded with robes, horses, and gifts, and the honor was announced throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 賀上表請代，朝議以賀得民情，不許。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial asking to be replaced; court discussion held that He had won the people's hearts, and permission was denied.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to be relieved of his post, but the court held that he had won the people's affection and refused.

sentences.zh: 在州七年，乃徵拜太尉。

translations.literal: After seven years in the province he was summoned and appointed Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: After seven years in the province he was recalled and appointed grand commander.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕寇邊，賀從駕追討，破之。

translations.literal: The Rouran raided the frontier; He followed the imperial carriage in pursuit and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Rouran raided the frontier he joined the emperor's pursuit and routed them.

sentences.zh: 顯祖將傳位于京兆王子推，時賀都督諸軍屯漠南，乃馳傳徵賀。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu was about to pass the throne to Zituo, Prince of Jingzhao; at the time He was supervising all armies encamped south of the desert, and an urgent dispatch summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzu prepared to abdicate in favor of Zituo, Prince of Jingzhao, He was commanding the armies south of the desert and was summoned by urgent dispatch.

sentences.zh: 賀既至，乃命公卿議之。

translations.literal: When He arrived, he ordered the nobles and ministers to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: When He arrived, the emperor ordered the high officials to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 賀正色固執不可。

translations.literal: He with stern countenance firmly held that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke with grave insistence that the plan must not proceed.

sentences.zh: 即詔賀持節奉皇帝璽綬以授高祖。

translations.literal: Immediately an edict ordered He to bear the staff of authority and present the imperial seal and cord to Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered He to bear the imperial credentials and present the seal and cord to Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 是歲，河西敕勒叛，遣賀率眾討之，降二千餘落，倍道兼行，追賊黨郁朱于等至枹罕，大破之，斬首五千餘級，虜男女萬餘口、雜畜三萬餘頭。

translations.literal: That year the Tiele of Hexi rebelled; He was sent leading troops to suppress them, receiving the submission of more than two thousand households; marching day and night he pursued the bandit party Yuzhuyu and others to Fuhan, inflicting a great defeat, beheading more than five thousand, capturing over ten thousand men and women, and over thirty thousand head of mixed livestock.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Tiele of Hexi rebelled. He led a force against them and received the submission of more than two thousand households. Forcing the pace, he pursued Yuzhuyu and his fellows to Fuhan, won a great victory, took more than five thousand heads, and captured over ten thousand men and women and more than thirty thousand head of livestock.

sentences.zh: 復追統萬、高平、上邽三鎮叛敕勒至于金城，斬首三千級。

translations.literal: He again pursued the rebel Tiele of the three garrisons Tongwan, Gaoping, and Shanggui as far as Jincheng, beheading three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to pursue rebel Tiele from the garrisons of Tongwan, Gaoping, and Shanggui as far as Jincheng and took three thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 賀依古今兵法及先儒耆舊之說，略採至要，為十二陳圖以上之。

translations.literal: He, relying on ancient and modern military methods and the teachings of former scholars and elders, briefly selected the essentials and made twelve battle-array diagrams which he presented upward.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing on classical military texts and the teachings of earlier strategists, he distilled the essentials into twelve battle-array diagrams and presented them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 顯祖覽而嘉焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu read them and praised them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu read them with approval.

sentences.zh: 賀以年老辭位，詔不許。

translations.literal: He, citing old age, resigned his post; the edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire on account of age, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 又詔都督三道諸軍，屯于漠南。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to supervise all armies of the three routes, encamped south of the desert.
translations.idiomatic: He was again ordered to command the three frontier armies encamped south of the desert.

sentences.zh: 是時，每歲秋冬，遣軍三道並出，以備北寇，至春中乃班師。

translations.literal: At that time every autumn and winter armies of three routes were sent out together to guard against northern enemies, and only by mid-spring did they withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Each autumn and winter three armies marched out together against the northern foe and did not return until spring.

sentences.zh: 賀以勞役京都，又非禦邊長計，乃上言：「請募諸州鎮有武健者三萬人，復其徭賦，厚加賑恤，分為三部。

translations.literal: He, considering that corvée exhausted the capital and that this was no long-term plan for defending the frontier, submitted: "I request recruiting thirty thousand able-bodied men from the provinces and garrisons, remitting their corvée and taxes, granting generous relief, and dividing them into three divisions.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that the campaigns wore out the capital and were no lasting defense of the frontier, and proposed: "Recruit thirty thousand able men from the provinces and garrisons, exempt them from corvée and taxes, grant them generous support, and divide them into three corps.

sentences.zh: 二鎮之間築城，城置萬人，給強弩十二床，武衞三百乘。

translations.literal: Between every two garrisons build a fort, each fort holding ten thousand men, supplied with twelve powerful crossbows and three hundred war chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Build a fort between each pair of garrisons, garrison each with ten thousand men, and equip each with twelve heavy crossbows and three hundred war carts.

sentences.zh: 弩一床，給牛六頭；

translations.literal: For each crossbow, supply six oxen;
translations.idiomatic: Each crossbow would require six oxen;

sentences.zh: 武衞一乘，給牛二頭。

translations.literal: for each war chariot, supply two oxen.
translations.idiomatic: each war cart, two oxen.

sentences.zh: 多造馬槍及諸器械，使武略大將二人以鎮撫之。

translations.literal: Make many horse-lances and various weapons, and appoint two great generals of martial strategy to pacify and oversee them.
translations.idiomatic: Stockpile lances and other arms, and place two seasoned generals in command of each district.

sentences.zh: 冬則講武，春則種殖，並戍並耕，則兵未勞而有盈畜矣。

translations.literal: In winter drill in arms, in spring plant crops—garrisoning and farming together, the troops would not be worn yet stores would be full.
translations.idiomatic: They would drill in winter and farm in spring, standing guard and tilling together, so the army would not be exhausted yet stores would overflow.

sentences.zh: 又於白道南三處立倉，運近州鎮租粟以充之，足食足兵，以備不虞，於宜為便。

translations.literal: Further, establish three granaries south of the White Road, transporting rent grain from nearby provinces and garrisons to fill them—sufficient food and sufficient troops to meet the unexpected; this would be convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Establish three granaries south of the White Road and ship grain from nearby provinces to fill them. With full stores and a standing force ready for any emergency, the frontier would be secure at far less cost.

sentences.zh: 不可歲常舉眾，連動京師，令朝庭恒有北顧之慮也。」

translations.literal: One cannot every year raise the host and continually stir the capital, keeping the court forever anxious toward the north."
translations.idiomatic: The court should not have to mobilize the capital every year and live in perpetual fear of the northern frontier."

sentences.zh: 事寢不報。

translations.literal: The matter slept without response.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was shelved without reply.

sentences.zh: 又上書稱病篤，乞骸骨，至于再三，乃許之。

translations.literal: He again memorialized claiming grave illness and begging his bones; only after repeating it again and again was permission granted.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again, declaring himself gravely ill and begging to retire; only after repeated pleas was he released.

sentences.zh: 朝有大議皆就詢訪，又給衣藥珍羞。

translations.literal: When the court had great deliberations he was always consulted; he was also given robes, medicines, and delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: On weighty matters of state the court still sought his counsel, and he was supplied with robes, medicines, and fine foods.

sentences.zh: 太和元年二月，療疾於溫湯，高祖、文明太后遣使者屢問消息，太醫視疾。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Taihe he took the cure at hot springs; Emperor Gaozu and Empress Dowager Wenming sent envoys repeatedly to inquire after him, and the imperial physicians attended his illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Taihe 1 he took the waters at the hot springs. Emperor Gaozu and Empress Dowager Wenming sent envoys repeatedly to inquire after him, and court physicians attended him.

sentences.zh: 患篤，還京師。

translations.literal: His illness grew grave and he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness worsened he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 賀乃遺令敕諸子曰：「吾頃以老患辭事，不悟天慈降恩，爵逮於汝。

translations.literal: He then left testamentary instructions charging his sons: "I recently resigned office because of old age and illness, not realizing Heaven's kindness would descend—rank reaching even to you.
translations.idiomatic: He left final instructions to his sons: "I resigned not long ago on account of age and illness, never imagining that Heaven's grace would extend so far that rank would reach even to you.

sentences.zh: 汝其毋傲吝，毋荒怠，毋奢越，毋嫉妬；

translations.literal: You must not be arrogant or stingy, must not be dissolute or negligent, must not be extravagant or overstep, must not be jealous;
translations.idiomatic: Be neither arrogant nor miserly, neither dissolute nor idle, neither extravagant nor presumptuous, neither envious nor spiteful;

sentences.zh: 疑思問，言思審，行思恭，服思度；

translations.literal: in doubt think and ask, in speech think and examine, in conduct think and be respectful, in dress think and measure;
translations.idiomatic: when in doubt, think and ask; in speech, think and weigh your words; in conduct, think and act with respect; in dress, think and keep within your station;

sentences.zh: 遏惡揚善，親賢遠佞；

translations.literal: restrain evil and exalt good, be close to the worthy and distant from flatterers;
translations.idiomatic: restrain evil and promote good, draw near to the worthy and keep flatterers at a distance;

sentences.zh: 目觀必真，耳屬必正；

translations.literal: what the eye sees must be true, what the ear attends must be upright;
translations.idiomatic: let the eye see truly and the ear listen rightly;

sentences.zh: 誠勤以事君，清約以行己。

translations.literal: serve the ruler with sincerity and diligence, conduct yourself with purity and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: serve your lord with sincerity and diligence, and conduct yourselves with purity and restraint.

sentences.zh: 吾終之後，所葬時服單櫝，足申孝心，芻靈明器，一無用也。」

translations.literal: After my end, bury me in the seasonal garments of a single coffin—enough to express filial heart; straw figures and bright vessels are wholly useless."
translations.idiomatic: When I am gone, bury me in my ordinary clothes in a plain coffin—that is filial piety enough. Straw figures and grave goods are of no use whatsoever."

sentences.zh: 三年秋薨，年七十三。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year he died; age seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the third year he died, aged seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、太尉、隴西王印綬，諡曰宣，賻雜綵五百匹，賜轀輬車及命服、溫明祕器，陪葬于金陵。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Commander, and the seal and cord of Prince of Longxi; posthumous title Xuan; funeral gifts of five hundred bolts of mixed silks; granted the imperial bier carriage, court robes, and the secret vessels Wenming; buried by accompaniment at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made attendant-in-ordinary and grand commander, with the seal and cord of Prince of Longxi, and given the posthumous title Xuan. Five hundred bolts of mixed silks were sent as funeral gifts, together with an imperial bier, court robes, and secret burial vessels; he was buried by accompaniment at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 長子延，性謹厚好學。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yan was by nature prudent, thick, and fond of learning.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yan was prudent, steady, and devoted to learning.

sentences.zh: 初以功臣子拜侍御中散，賜爵武城子，西冶都將。

translations.literal: At first, as son of a meritorious minister he was appointed Attendant Censor in the Imperial Secretariat, granted the title Baron of Wucheng, and made Commandant of the Western Foundry.
translations.idiomatic: At first, as the son of a meritorious minister, he was made attendant censor in the imperial secretariat, enfeoffed as Baron of Wucheng, and appointed commandant of the western foundry.

sentences.zh: [3]卒，贈涼州刺史、廣武侯，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: [3] He died; posthumously he was given Inspector of Liangzhou and Marquis of Guangwu; posthumous title Jian.
translations.idiomatic: [3] He died and was posthumously made inspector of Liangzhou and Marquis of Guangwu, with the posthumous title Jian.

sentences.zh: 子鱗襲。

translations.literal: His son Lin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lin inherited his rank.

sentences.zh: 延弟思禮，後賜名懷，謙恭寬雅，有大度。

translations.literal: Yan's younger brother Silu, later granted the name Huai, was modest, respectful, broad, and elegant, with great magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's younger brother Silu, later given the name Huai, was modest, gracious, and magnanimous.

sentences.zh: 高宗末，為侍御中散。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Wencheng's reign he was Attendant Censor in the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Emperor Wencheng's reign he served as attendant censor in the imperial secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父賀辭老，詔懷受父爵，拜征南將軍。

translations.literal: When his father He resigned on account of age, an edict ordered Huai to receive his father's title and appointed him General Who Campaigns South.
translations.idiomatic: When his father He retired, an edict had Huai inherit his father's title and appointed him general who campaigns south.

sentences.zh: 尋為持節、督諸軍，屯於漠南。

translations.literal: Soon he bore the staff of authority and supervised all armies, encamped south of the desert.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was given imperial credentials and command of the armies south of the desert.

sentences.zh: 還，除殿中尚書，出為長安鎮將、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: On return he was made Director of the Palace Secretariat, then sent out as Garrison Commander of Chang'an and Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made director of the palace secretariat, then sent out as garrison commander of Chang'an and inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 清儉有惠政，善於撫恤，劫盜息止，流民皆相率來還。

translations.literal: Frugal and clean, he had benevolent governance, was skilled in comforting and relief; banditry ceased, and displaced people all came back in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with frugality and kindness, comforted the people well, and banditry ceased; refugees returned in droves.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，復拜殿中尚書，加侍中，參都曹事。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was again appointed Director of the Palace Secretariat, added as Attendant-in-Ordinary, and participated in the affairs of the central secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was again made director of the palace secretariat and attendant-in-ordinary, and took part in central administration.

sentences.zh: 又督諸軍征蠕蠕，六道大將咸受節度。

translations.literal: He again supervised all armies in the campaign against the Rouran; the great generals of six routes all received his command.
translations.idiomatic: He again commanded the armies against the Rouran, and the six route commanders all served under him.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書令，參議律令。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing and participated in deliberating statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the masters of writing and helped draft laws and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 後例降為公。

translations.literal: Later by precedent he was reduced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: Later, by precedent, his princely rank was reduced to duke.

sentences.zh: 除司州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Inspector of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed inspector of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 從駕南征，加衞大將軍，領中軍事。

translations.literal: He followed the imperial carriage on the southern campaign, was added as Grand General of the Guard, and headed central military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern campaign he was made grand general of the guard and placed in charge of central military affairs.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職，賜帛三百匹、穀千石。

translations.literal: He left office on account of mourning for his mother and was granted three hundred bolts of silk and a thousand piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother and was granted three hundred bolts of silk and a thousand piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 十九年，除征北大將軍、夏州刺史，轉都督雍岐東秦諸軍事、征西大將軍、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was appointed Grand General Who Campaigns North and Inspector of Xiazhou, then transferred to supervise military affairs of Yong, Qi, and Eastern Qin, Grand General Who Campaigns West, and Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was made grand general who campaigns north and inspector of Xiazhou, then transferred to supervise military affairs in Yong, Qi, and eastern Qin, and made grand general who campaigns west and inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 景明二年，徵為尚書左僕射，加特進。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingming he was summoned as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and granted extraordinary advancement.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingming 2 he was recalled as left vice director of the masters of writing and granted extraordinary advancement.

sentences.zh: 時有詔，以姦吏犯罪，每多逃遁，因眚乃出，並皆釋然。

translations.literal: At the time there was an edict that because corrupt officials who committed crimes often fled and hid, only emerging when amnesties were proclaimed, all were to be released.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then declared that corrupt officials who fled when charged would all be released whenever a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 自今已後，犯罪不問輕重，而藏竄者悉遠流。

translations.literal: From now on, regardless of the gravity of the crime, all who hid and fled were to be banished far away.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, regardless of the gravity of the offense, all who fled and hid were to be exiled to distant regions.

sentences.zh: 若永避不出，兄弟代徙。

translations.literal: If they forever avoided and did not emerge, brothers would be sent in their place.
translations.idiomatic: If they never came forward, their brothers would be sent into exile in their stead.

sentences.zh: 懷乃奏曰：「謹按條制：逃吏不在赦限。

translations.literal: Huai then memorialized: "I respectfully examine the regulations: fugitive officials are not within the scope of amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Huai memorialized: "The regulations provide that fugitive officials are not within the scope of amnesty.

sentences.zh: 竊惟聖朝之恩，事異前宥，諸流徙在路，尚蒙旋反，況有未發而仍遣邊戍？

translations.literal: I reflect that the grace of the sage court differs from former pardons—those banished on the road still receive permission to return; how much more those who have not yet fled but are still sent to border garrisons?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the grace of this court differs from earlier pardons: exiles already on the road are allowed to return—how much less should those not yet fled be sent to the frontier?

sentences.zh: 按守宰犯罪，逃走者眾，祿潤既優，尚有茲失，及蒙恩宥，卒然得還。

translations.literal: Consider that among prefects and magistrates who commit crimes, many flee; their salaries and benefits being ample, they still have such failures, yet when they receive grace and pardon they suddenly return.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and magistrates who commit crimes often flee, yet with their generous salaries they are pardoned and suddenly restored.

sentences.zh: 今獨苦此等，恐非均一之法。

translations.literal: Now to afflict only this class—I fear this is not a uniform law.
translations.idiomatic: To punish only the lower ranks while sparing the higher would not be equal justice.

sentences.zh: 如臣管執，謂宜免之。」

translations.literal: In your servant's narrow view, I say it should be waived."
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view this measure should be withdrawn."

sentences.zh: 書奏，門下以成式既班，駁奏不許。

translations.literal: When the memorial was presented, the Secretariat, holding that the established form had already been promulgated, rejected the memorial and did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was rejected by the secretariat on the grounds that the new rule had already been promulgated.

sentences.zh: 懷重奏曰：「臣以為法貴經通，治尚簡要，刑憲之設，所以網羅罪人。

translations.literal: Huai memorialized again: "Your servant holds that law values constancy and penetration, governance values simplicity, and the establishment of punishments and statutes is to net wrongdoers.
translations.idiomatic: Huai memorialized again: "Law should be steady and clear, governance simple; punishments exist to catch wrongdoers.

sentences.zh: 苟理之所備，不在繁典；

translations.literal: If reason is fully provided, it lies not in prolix codes;
translations.idiomatic: When principle is fully served, prolix codes are unnecessary;

sentences.zh: 行之可通，豈容峻制。

translations.literal: if practice can penetrate, how can harsh systems be tolerated?
translations.idiomatic: when practice can proceed smoothly, harsh systems have no place.

sentences.zh: 此乃古今之達政，救世之恒規。

translations.literal: This is the penetrating governance of ancient and modern times, the constant rule for saving the age.
translations.idiomatic: This has been sound governance in every age and the constant rule of humane rule.

sentences.zh: 伏尋條制，勳品已下，罪發逃亡，遇恩不宥，仍流妻子。

translations.literal: I bow and examine the regulations: below the rank of meritorious grade, when crimes are exposed and they flee, meeting grace they are not pardoned and wives and children are still banished.
translations.idiomatic: The regulations provide that officials below meritorious rank who flee when charged are denied amnesty and their wives and children are banished.

sentences.zh: 雖欲抑絕姦途，匪為通式。

translations.literal: Though wishing to cut off the path of wickedness, this is not a universal pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Though meant to cut off corruption, this is no universal rule.

sentences.zh: 謹按事條，侵官敗法，專據流外，豈九品已上，人皆貞白也？

translations.literal: I respectfully examine the articles: usurping office and violating law are solely placed outside the stream—are all men of the ninth rank and above pure and white?
translations.idiomatic: Usurpation and violation of law are punished—but are all officials of the ninth rank and above pure?

sentences.zh: 其諸州守宰，職任清流，至有貪濁，事發逃竄，而遇恩免罪。

translations.literal: The prefects and magistrates of the various provinces, whose offices are pure streams, even reach greed and corruption; when matters are exposed they flee and hide, yet meeting grace they escape punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and magistrates of pure-stream offices grow corrupt, flee when exposed, yet escape punishment through amnesty.

sentences.zh: 勳品已下，獨乖斯例。

translations.literal: Below meritorious grade alone violates this pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Only those below meritorious rank suffer the harsher rule.

sentences.zh: 如此，則寬縱上流，法切下吏，育物有差，惠罸不等。

translations.literal: Thus the upper stream is lenient and indulgent while the law is harsh on lower officials—nurturing things has disparity, grace and punishment are unequal.
translations.idiomatic: The high are indulged while the low are harshly punished—favor and penalty are unequal.

sentences.zh: 又謀逆滔天，輕恩尚免，[4]吏犯微罪，獨不蒙赦，使大宥之經不通，開生之路致壅，進違古典，退乖今律，輒率愚見，以為宜停。」

translations.literal: Further, for treason reaching to heaven, light grace still grants exemption;[4] officials guilty of slight crimes alone do not receive pardon—making the great pardon canon not penetrate and the road of giving life blocked; advancing it violates ancient models, retreating it contradicts present statutes—I rashly lead my foolish view and hold it should be stopped."
translations.idiomatic: Treason against heaven itself may be pardoned,[4] yet minor official offenses alone are denied amnesty, blocking the great pardon and choking off mercy. This violates ancient precedent and present law alike. I humbly urge that it be withdrawn."

sentences.zh: 書奏，世宗納之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was presented, Emperor Shizong adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong accepted the memorial.

sentences.zh: 其年，除車騎大將軍、涼州大中正。

translations.literal: That year he was appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Chief Rectifier of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was made grand general of chariots and cavalry and chief rectifier of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 懷奏曰：「南賊遊魂江揚，職為亂逆，肆厥淫昏，月滋日甚，貴臣重將，靡有孑遺，崇信姦回，昵比閹豎，內外離心，骨肉猜叛。

translations.literal: Huai memorialized: "The southern bandits, wandering souls on the Jiang and Yang, by office are rebels and traitors; they indulge their lewdness and folly, month by month and day by day growing worse; noble ministers and great generals, not one spared; they honor faith in treacherous villains and draw close to eunuch attendants; inside and outside lose heart, flesh and bone suspect and rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Huai memorialized: "The southern regime wanders like a ghost along the Yangzi. Its rulers are rebels who grow more dissolute by the day. Noble ministers and great generals have been destroyed without exception. They trust villains and dote on eunuchs; court and country are divided, kin turn against kin.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶融僭號於荊郢，其雍州刺史蕭衍勒兵而東襲，上流之眾已逼其郊。

translations.literal: Xiao Baorong usurped title at Jing and Ying; his Inspector of Yongzhou Xiao Yan marshaled troops and struck eastward; the hosts of the upper reaches already pressed their suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Baorong has set up a rival court in Jing and Ying, while his inspector of Yongzhou Xiao Yan marches east with an army and forces from the upper Yangzi already press the capital's outskirts.

sentences.zh: 廣陵、京口各持兵而懷兩望，鍾離、淮陰並鼎峙而觀得失。

translations.literal: Guangling and Jingkou each held troops and harbored two hopes; Zhongli and Huaiyin both stood like tripods watching success and failure.
translations.idiomatic: Guangling and Jingkou hold their armies and wait to see which side wins; Zhongli and Huaiyin stand like rival poles watching the outcome.

sentences.zh: 秣陵孤危，制不出門。

translations.literal: Moling was isolated and perilous; control did not extend beyond the gates.
translations.idiomatic: Moling stands isolated and helpless, its rulers powerless beyond the city gates.

sentences.zh: 君子小人，並罹災禍，延首北望，朝不及夕。

translations.literal: Gentleman and petty man alike suffered disaster; craning their necks they looked north, morning not reaching evening.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle and simple alike suffer disaster, craning their necks toward the north, their deliverance uncertain from one day to the next.

sentences.zh: 斯實天啟之期，吞并之會。

translations.literal: This is truly the season Heaven opens and the occasion for swallowing and merging.
translations.idiomatic: This is truly the season Heaven has opened for conquest and union.

sentences.zh: 乘厥蕭牆之釁，藉其分崩之隙，東據歷陽，兼指瓜步，緣江鎮戍，達於荊郢。

translations.literal: Riding their trouble within the palace walls, borrowing the gap of their splitting apart, seize Liyang in the east and also point at Guabu; along the river establish garrison posts reaching to Jing and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Seize the turmoil within their walls and the cracks in their unity: hold Liyang in the east, threaten Guabu, and plant garrisons along the river as far as Jing and Ying.

sentences.zh: 然後奮雷電之威，布山河之信，則江西之地，不刃自來，吳會之鄉，指期可舉。

translations.literal: Then exert the might of thunder and lightning, spread the faith of mountains and rivers—then the lands west of the river will come without a blade, and the districts of Wu and Kuai may be raised within a set term.
translations.idiomatic: Then strike with thunderous force and proclaim your faith across the land—the region west of the river will submit without a blow, and Wu and Kuai will fall within reach.

sentences.zh: 昔士治有言，皓若暴死，更立賢主，文武之官，各得其任，則勁敵也。

translations.literal: Formerly Shi Zhi said: if Hao died suddenly and a worthy ruler were established, civil and military officials each obtaining their posts, then they would be a strong foe.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhi once said that if Sun Hao died suddenly and a worthy ruler took the throne with able ministers in their posts, Wu would be a formidable foe again.

sentences.zh: 若蕭衍克就，上下同心，非直後圖之難，實亦揚境危逼。

translations.literal: If Xiao Yan succeeds and above and below share one heart, it is not only that later plans would be hard—truly the Yang region borders would be perilously pressed.
translations.idiomatic: If Xiao Yan succeeds and unites the court, not only will later conquest grow harder—the Yangzhou frontier itself will be gravely threatened.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 壽春之去建鄴，七百而已，山川水陸，彼所諳利。

translations.literal: From Shouchun to Jianye is only seven hundred li; mountains, rivers, water, and land—they are skilled in their advantages.
translations.idiomatic: Shouchun lies only seven hundred li from Jianye, over terrain they know by water and land alike.

sentences.zh: 脫江湘無波，君臣效職，藉水憑舟，倐忽而至，壽春容不自保，江南將若之何？

translations.literal: If the Jiang and Xiang were without waves, ruler and ministers fulfilling their duties, relying on water and boats, they would arrive in a flash—Shouchun could hardly preserve itself; what would become of the lands south of the river?
translations.idiomatic: If the rivers were calm and ruler and ministers united, they could come by water in a flash. Shouchun could not hold, and what then for the south?

sentences.zh: 今寶卷邑居有土崩之形，邊城無繼援之兆，清蕩江區，實在今日。

translations.literal: Now Baojuan's seat has the form of landslide collapse; border cities have no sign of continuing relief—the clear sweeping of the river region truly lies in today.
translations.idiomatic: Baojuan's throne already totters; border cities have no hope of relief. To sweep the Yangzi region clean must be done now.

sentences.zh: 臣受恩既重，不敢不言。」

translations.literal: Your servant has received grace already heavy and dares not fail to speak."
translations.idiomatic: I have received such great favor that I dare not remain silent."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「不君不臣，江南常弊，有粟不食，其在斯矣。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Neither ruler nor minister—the constant failing of Jiangnan; having grain yet not eating—here it lies.
translations.idiomatic: The edict replied: "The south's constant failing is that it has neither true ruler nor true minister—grain in the storehouses yet none to govern. That is the case here.

sentences.zh: 上天將欲亡之，諸蕃又願取之，人事天道，孰云匪會？

translations.literal: Heaven above wishes to destroy them; the various realms also wish to take them—human affairs and Heaven's Way, who says they do not meet?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven wishes to destroy them and every border state would seize them—human affairs and Heaven's way, who can say they do not coincide?

sentences.zh: 但以養害，仁者不為。

translations.literal: Yet to nurture harm—a benevolent man does not do this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to nurture harm for one's own gain—a benevolent ruler will not do it.

sentences.zh: 且十月五日，衍軍已達大航，其大傷小亡之勢，久應有決。

translations.literal: Moreover, on the fifth day of the tenth month Yan's army had already reached Dahang; the momentum of the great injuring the small and the small perishing should long ago have had a decision.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, on the fifth of the tenth month Yan's army had already reached Dahang. The great crushing the small should long since have reached its outcome.

sentences.zh: 假令天罰寶卷，衍兵獲進，則衍之主佐，又是亂亡遺孽，皇靈其能久祐之乎？

translations.literal: Suppose Heaven punishes Baojuan and Yan's troops advance—then Yan's ruler and assistants are again remnants of chaos and ruin; can the imperial numen long protect them?
translations.idiomatic: Even if Heaven punishes Baojuan and Yan advances, Yan and his followers are themselves remnants of a doomed regime—can the imperial spirit long protect them?

sentences.zh: 今之所矜者，正以南黔企德，邊書繼至，殄悴之氓，理須救接。

translations.literal: What we now pity is precisely that the southern common people look to our virtue; border reports come in succession; the perishing and wasted folk by reason must be rescued and received.
translations.idiomatic: What we must pity now is that the southern people look to our virtue; border reports come in succession, and these wasted folk must be rescued.

sentences.zh: 若爾者，揚州兵力，配積不少，但可速遣任城，委以處分，別加慰勉，令妙盡邊算也。」

translations.literal: If so, Yangzhou's military strength, allocated and accumulated, is not small—only speedily send the Prince of Rencheng, entrust disposal to him, separately add comfort and encouragement, and order him to exhaust border stratagems."
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou has no lack of troops. Send the Prince of Rencheng at once, entrust the frontier to him, encourage him well, and let him carry out the border strategy to the full."

sentences.zh: 以衍事克，遂停。

translations.literal: Because Yan's affair succeeded, it was then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan succeeded, the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 懷又表曰：「昔世祖昇遐，南安在位，出拜東廟，為賊臣宗愛所弒。

translations.literal: Huai again memorialized: "Formerly when Emperor Taiwu ascended afar, the Prince of Nan'an held the throne; going out to worship the Eastern Temple he was assassinated by the traitor minister Zong'ai.
translations.idiomatic: Huai memorialized again: "When Emperor Taiwu died, the Prince of Nan'an held the throne. Going out to worship at the Eastern Temple, he was murdered by the traitor Zong'ai.

sentences.zh: 時高宗避難，龍潛苑中，宗愛異圖，神位未定。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Wencheng took refuge from disaster, the dragon hidden in the park; Zong'ai had divergent designs and the divine seat was not settled.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wencheng was in hiding in the imperial park while Zong'ai plotted and the throne stood vacant.

sentences.zh: 臣亡父先臣賀與長孫渴侯、陸麗等表迎高宗，[5]纂徽寶命。

translations.literal: Your servant's deceased father, the former minister He, with Zhangsun Kehou, Lu Li, and others memorialized to welcome Emperor Wencheng,[5] succeeding to the august mandate.
translations.idiomatic: My late father He, with Zhangsun Kehou, Lu Li, and others, memorialized to welcome Emperor Wencheng[5] and secure the imperial mandate.

sentences.zh: 麗以扶負聖躬，親所見識，蒙授撫軍大將軍、司徒公、平原王。

translations.literal: Li, for supporting the sacred person with his own eyes witnessed, received appointment as General Who Pacifies the Army, Duke of the Masses, and Prince of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li, who had borne the emperor in his own arms, was made general who pacifies the army, duke of the masses, and Prince of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 興安二年，追論定策之勳，進先臣爵西平王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xing'an, tracing merit in settling the succession, the former minister's title was advanced to Prince of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: In Xing'an 2, for his role in securing the succession, my father was advanced to Prince of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 皇興季年，顯祖將傳大位於京兆王。

translations.literal: In the last year of Huangxing, Emperor Xianzu was about to transmit the great seat to the Prince of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the last year of Huangxing, Emperor Xianzu prepared to pass the throne to the Prince of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 先臣時都督諸將，屯於武川，被徵詣京，特見顧問。

translations.literal: The former minister then supervised all generals, encamped at Wuchuan, was summoned to the capital, and was specially granted audience and consultation.
translations.idiomatic: My father then commanded the armies at Wuchuan, was summoned to the capital, and received special audience.

sentences.zh: 先臣固執不可，顯祖久乃許之，遂命先臣持節授皇帝璽綬於高祖。

translations.literal: The former minister firmly held it could not be done; only after long time did Emperor Xianzu consent, then ordered the former minister to bear the staff and present the imperial seal and cord to Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: My father firmly opposed the plan until Emperor Xianzu at last agreed, and ordered him to present the imperial seal and cord to Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 至太和十六年，麗息叡狀秘書，[6]稱其亡父與先臣援立高宗，朝廷追錄，封叡鉅鹿郡開國公。

translations.literal: By the sixteenth year of Taihe, Li's son Rui submitted a memorial to the Secretariat,[6] stating that his deceased father with the former minister had aided in establishing Emperor Wencheng; the court traced the record and enfeoffed Rui as Duke of Julu commandery with a state fief.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 16, Li's son Rui submitted a memorial[6] claiming that his father and mine had together placed Emperor Wencheng on the throne. The court reviewed the record and enfeoffed Rui as Duke of Julu with a state fief.

sentences.zh: 臣時丁艱草土，不容及例。

translations.literal: Your servant was then in mourning on raw earth and could not reach the precedent.
translations.idiomatic: I was then in mourning and could not press my claim.

sentences.zh: 至二十年，除臣雍州刺史，臨發奉辭，面奏先帝，申先臣舊勳。

translations.literal: By the twentieth year your servant was appointed Inspector of Yongzhou; on the eve of departure, presenting farewell, he memorialized the late emperor face to face, stating the former minister's old merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year I was appointed inspector of Yongzhou. On departing I addressed the late emperor in person and pleaded my father's old service.

sentences.zh: 時敕旨但赴所臨，尋當別判。

translations.literal: At the time the imperial order said only to go to one's post; soon there would be separate judgment.
translations.idiomatic: I was told only to proceed to my post and that judgment would follow.

sentences.zh: 至二十一年，車駕幸雍，臣復陳聞，時蒙敕旨，征還當授。

translations.literal: By the twenty-first year the imperial carriage visited Yong; your servant again stated the matter and then received the imperial order that on recall he would be granted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, when the emperor visited Yong, I raised the matter again and was told that on my recall I would receive my due.

sentences.zh: 自宮車晏駕，遂爾不白。

translations.literal: Since the palace carriage peacefully departed, it has thus not been reported.
translations.idiomatic: Since the emperor's death I have not been able to press my claim.

sentences.zh: 竊惟先臣遠則援立高宗，寶曆不墜；

translations.literal: I reflect that the former minister, in the distant past, aided in establishing Emperor Wencheng and the precious succession did not fall;
translations.idiomatic: My father, in the distant past, helped place Emperor Wencheng on the throne and preserved the dynasty;

sentences.zh: 近則陳力顯祖，神器有歸。

translations.literal: in the near past he displayed his strength for Emperor Xianzu and the divine vessel had its return.
translations.idiomatic: in recent times he served Emperor Xianzu and secured the transfer of the throne.

sentences.zh: 如斯之勳，超世之事。

translations.literal: Merit such as this is a matter transcending the age.
translations.idiomatic: Such service transcends ordinary merit.

sentences.zh: 麗以父功而獲河山之賞，[7]臣有家勳，不霑茅社之賜。

translations.literal: Li by his father's merit received reward of mountains and rivers;[7] your servant has family merit yet has not touched the grant of fief altars.
translations.idiomatic: Li received a state fief for his father's service,[7] yet I, with equal family merit, have received no such grant.

sentences.zh: 得否相懸，請垂裁處。」

translations.literal: Gain and denial hang apart—I beg you to let fall judgment and disposition."
translations.idiomatic: The disparity is unjust. I beg your judgment."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「宿老元丕，云如所訴，訪之史官，頗亦言此。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The veteran Yuan Pi says as you plead; inquiring of the historiographers, many also speak of this.
translations.idiomatic: The edict replied: "The veteran Yuan Pi confirms your account, and the historiographers largely agree.

sentences.zh: 可依比授馮翊郡開國公，邑百戶。」

translations.literal: You may be granted by parallel Duke of Fengyi commandery with a state fief, a fief of one hundred households."
translations.idiomatic: You are accordingly enfeoffed as Duke of Fengyi with a state fief of one hundred households."

translations.literal: End of edict.
translations.idiomatic: End of edict.

sentences.zh: 又詔為使持節，加侍中、行臺，巡行北邊六鎮、恒燕朔三州，賑給貧乏，兼採風俗，考論殿最，事之得失，皆先決後聞。

translations.literal: He was again ordered as envoy bearing the staff of authority, added as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Mobile Secretariat, to tour the six northern garrisons and the three provinces of Heng, Yan, and Shuo, relieve the poor and needy, and also gather customs, assess excellence in office, and the gains and losses of affairs—all decided first, then reported.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made envoy with imperial credentials, attendant-in-ordinary, and mobile secretariat, to tour the six northern garrisons and the provinces of Heng, Yan, and Shuo, relieve the poor, examine local customs, and assess officials—all to be decided on the spot and reported afterward.

sentences.zh: 自京師遷洛，邊朔遙遠，加連年旱儉，百姓困弊。

translations.literal: Since the capital moved from Pingcheng to Luoyang, the northern frontier was far away, and with successive years of drought and famine the common people were distressed and exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Since the move from Pingcheng to Luoyang the northern frontier had grown remote, and years of drought had left the people in desperate want.

sentences.zh: 懷銜命巡撫，存恤有方，便宜運轉，有無通濟。

translations.literal: Huai bore the mandate on his tour of comfort; his relief had method, and expedient transport moved goods so that presence and absence were mutually aided.
translations.idiomatic: Huai carried out his mission with skill, relieving distress effectively and moving supplies so that want and plenty were balanced.

sentences.zh: 時后父于勁勢傾朝野，勁兄于祚與懷宿昔通婚，時為沃野鎮將，頗有受納。

translations.literal: At the time the empress's father Yu Jin's power tilted court and countryside; Jin's elder brother Yu Zuo had long-standing marriage ties with Huai and was then Garrison Commander of Woye, with considerable taking of bribes.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's father Yu Jin then dominated the court. Jin's elder brother Yu Zuo, who had long been allied to Huai by marriage, was garrison commander of Woye and had taken many bribes.

sentences.zh: 懷將入鎮，祚郊迎道左，懷不與語，即劾祚免官。

translations.literal: As Huai was about to enter the garrison, Zuo met him in the suburbs on the left of the road; Huai did not speak with him and immediately impeached Zuo and removed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: As Huai entered the region, Zuo met him on the road; Huai would not speak with him and immediately impeached him and stripped him of office.

sentences.zh: 懷朔鎮將元尼須與懷少舊，亦貪穢狼藉，置酒請懷，謂懷曰：「命之長短，由卿之口，豈可不相寬貸？」

translations.literal: Yuan Nixu, Garrison Commander of Huaishuo, was an old acquaintance of Huai from youth and was also greedy and filthy beyond reckoning; he set out wine and invited Huai, saying: "Whether life is long or short is in your mouth—how can you not show mutual leniency?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Nixu, garrison commander of Huaishuo, was an old friend of Huai's youth and equally corrupt. He set out wine and said, "My fate is in your hands—surely you will show leniency?"

sentences.zh: 懷曰：「今日之集，乃是源懷與故人飲酒之坐，非鞫獄之所也。

translations.literal: Huai said: "Today's gathering is Yuan Huai drinking wine with an old friend—it is not the place for examining cases.
translations.idiomatic: Huai replied, "Today we are old friends drinking together—not holding court.

sentences.zh: 明日公庭，始為使人撿鎮將罪狀之處。」

translations.literal: Tomorrow in the public court is where the envoy first sorts the garrison commander's counts of crime."
translations.idiomatic: Tomorrow in open court I shall be the envoy examining a garrison commander's crimes."

sentences.zh: 尼須揮淚而已，無以對之。

translations.literal: Nixu could only wave away tears and had nothing with which to reply.
translations.idiomatic: Nixu could only weep and had no reply.

sentences.zh: 懷既而表劾尼須。

translations.literal: Huai afterward memorialized to impeach Nixu.
translations.idiomatic: Huai soon memorialized to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 其奉公不撓，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His serving the public without bending were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His integrity in public service was always of this sort.

sentences.zh: 懷又表曰：「景明以來，北蕃連年災旱，高原陸野，不任營殖，唯有水田，少可菑畝。

translations.literal: Huai again memorialized: "Since Jingming the northern frontier has suffered drought year after year; high plateau and dry land cannot support cultivation—only paddy fields allow some acres of planting.
translations.idiomatic: Huai memorialized again: "Since Jingming the north has suffered drought year after year. The high plateaus cannot be farmed; only paddy fields offer any harvest.

sentences.zh: 然主將參僚，專擅腴美，瘠土荒疇給百姓，因此困弊，日月滋甚。

translations.literal: Yet commanders and staff monopolize the rich and fine, giving lean soil and waste fields to the common people; thereby distress grows day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Yet commanders and their staffs seize the best land and leave only poor soil to the people, who grow poorer by the day.

sentences.zh: 諸鎮水田，請依地令分給細民，先貧後富，若分付不平，令一人怨訟者，鎮將已下連署之官，各奪一時之祿，四人已上奪祿一周。

translations.literal: The paddy fields of the various garrisons—I request distributing them to the common people according to the land ordinance, poor first then rich; if distribution is unfair and one man lodges complaint, the garrison commander and all co-signing officials below shall each lose one term's salary, four men and above lose one cycle of salary.
translations.idiomatic: I propose that garrison paddy fields be distributed to the people according to the land law, the poor first. If the distribution is unfair and even one man complains, the garrison commander and all signing officials shall forfeit one term's salary, or one full year's salary if four or more are involved.

sentences.zh: 北鎮邊蕃，事異諸夏，往日置官，全不差別。

translations.literal: The northern garrisons and frontier peoples differ in affairs from the central domains; formerly in establishing offices there was no distinction at all.
translations.idiomatic: The northern garrisons differ from the central provinces, yet offices were established without distinction.

sentences.zh: 沃野一鎮，自將已下八百餘人，黎庶怨嗟，僉曰煩猥。

translations.literal: At Woye garrison alone, from the commander down there were more than eight hundred men; the common people groaned and sighed, all saying it was vexatious and excessive.
translations.idiomatic: At Woye garrison alone there were more than eight hundred officials from the commander down, and the people universally complained of the burden.

sentences.zh: 邊隅事尠，實少畿服，請主帥吏佐五分減二。」

translations.literal: Frontier matters are few, truly lacking metropolitan service—I request reducing commanders and clerical assistants by two-fifths."
translations.idiomatic: Frontier duties are light and far from the capital; I propose reducing commanders and staff by two-fifths."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「省表具恤民之懷，已敕有司一依所上，下為永準。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Your memorial fully shows care for the people; I have ordered the relevant offices to follow entirely what you submitted, and promulgate it as permanent standard.
translations.idiomatic: The edict replied: "Your memorial shows genuine care for the people. The relevant offices are ordered to follow your proposals and make them permanent policy.

sentences.zh: 如斯之比，不便於民，損化害政者，其備列以聞。」

translations.literal: Matters of this kind inconvenient to the people and harming transformation and governance—fully list them and report."
translations.idiomatic: Report any similar measures that burden the people or harm good governance."

sentences.zh: 時細民為豪強陵壓，積年枉滯，一朝見申者，日有百數。

translations.literal: At the time common folk were oppressed by powerful families; wrongs piled up for years—those vindicated in a single day numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Common people long oppressed by powerful families saw hundreds of old wrongs redressed in a single day.

sentences.zh: 所上事宜便於北邊者，凡四十餘條，皆見嘉納。

translations.literal: Matters submitted convenient for the northern frontier numbered more than forty articles, all praised and adopted.
translations.idiomatic: More than forty proposals for the northern frontier were all praised and adopted.

sentences.zh: 正始元年九月，有告蠕蠕率十二萬騎六道並進，欲直趨沃野、懷朔，南寇恒代。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Zhengshi, it was reported that the Rouran led a hundred and twenty thousand horsemen in six routes advancing together, intending to rush straight to Woye and Huaishuo and raid south into Heng and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Zhengshi 1 it was reported that the Rouran were advancing with a hundred and twenty thousand horsemen in six columns toward Woye and Huaishuo, intending to raid Heng and Dai.

sentences.zh: 詔懷以本官，加使持節、侍中，出據北蕃，指授規略，隨須徵發，諸所處分皆以便宜從事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Huai with his existing office, added as envoy bearing the staff and Attendant-in-Ordinary, to go out and hold the northern frontier, assign strategy, mobilize as needed, and dispose of all matters by expedient authority.
translations.idiomatic: Huai was ordered to hold his existing post, made envoy with credentials and attendant-in-ordinary, sent to the northern frontier to direct strategy, mobilize troops as needed, and act on his own authority where expedient.

sentences.zh: 又詔懷子直寢徽隨懷北行。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered Huai's son Zhi and grandson Hui to accompany Huai north.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi and grandson Hui were ordered to accompany him north.

sentences.zh: 詔賜馬一匹、細鎧一具、御矟一枚。

translations.literal: An edict granted one horse, one suit of fine armor, and one imperial spear.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a horse, a suit of fine armor, and an imperial spear.

sentences.zh: 懷拜受訖，乃於其庭跨鞍執矟，躍馬大呼，顧謂賓客曰：「氣力雖衰，尚得如此。

translations.literal: Huai bowed and received them; then in his courtyard he mounted the saddle, grasped the spear, leaped the horse and shouted loudly, turning to tell his guests: "Though my strength declines, I can still do this.
translations.idiomatic: After receiving them he mounted in his courtyard, seized the spear, spurred his horse, and shouted to his guests, "My strength may be failing, but I can still do this.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕雖畏壯輕老，我亦未便可欺。

translations.literal: The Rouran may fear the strong and slight the old, but I am not yet to be fooled.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran may despise the old and fear the young, but they shall not find me easy prey.

sentences.zh: 今奉廟勝之規，總驍捍之眾，足以擒其酋帥，獻俘闕下耳。」

translations.literal: Now following the plan ordained in the temple, commanding fierce and brave hosts, it is enough to seize their chieftains and present captives below the palace gates."
translations.idiomatic: With the court's strategy behind me and brave troops at my command, I shall capture their chiefs and present them at the palace gates."

sentences.zh: 時年六十一。

translations.literal: He was then sixty-one years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was sixty-one years old.

sentences.zh: 懷至雲中，蠕蠕亡遁。

translations.literal: When Huai reached Yunzhong, the Rouran fled and vanished.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai reached Yunzhong the Rouran had already fled.

sentences.zh: 懷旋至恒代，案視諸鎮左右要害之地，可以築城置戍之處。

translations.literal: Huai returned to Heng and Dai and examined the vital points left and right of the various garrisons where forts and garrison posts could be built.
translations.idiomatic: On his return to Heng and Dai he surveyed the garrisons for sites where forts and posts could be built.

sentences.zh: 皆量其高下，揣其厚薄，及儲糧積仗之宜，犬牙相救之勢，凡表五十八條。

translations.literal: He measured their height and low, gauged their thickness, and the suitability of storing grain and accumulating weapons, and the posture of mutual rescue like dog's teeth—in all memorialized fifty-eight articles.
translations.idiomatic: He measured terrain, assessed defenses, planned grain stores and arms depots, and arranged mutual support between posts, memorializing fifty-eight proposals in all.

sentences.zh: 表曰：「蠕蠕不覊，自古而爾。

translations.literal: His memorial said: "The Rouran are unrestrained, thus from ancient times.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "The Rouran have never been tamed, from antiquity to the present.

sentences.zh: 遊魂鳥集，水草為家，中國患者，皆斯類耳。

translations.literal: Wandering souls gathering like birds, water and grass their home—all who afflict the central domains are of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: They wander like ghosts and birds, making their home in grass and water—all who plague the central realms are of this kind.

sentences.zh: 歷代驅逐，莫之能制。

translations.literal: Dynasty after dynasty drove them off yet could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: Dynasty after dynasty drove them off without mastering them.

sentences.zh: 雖北拓榆中，遠臨瀚海，而智臣勇將，力算俱竭，胡人頗遁，中國以疲。

translations.literal: Though the north was extended to Yuzhong and far gazed on the Han Sea, wise ministers and brave generals exhausted strength and stratagem alike; the barbarians largely escaped while the central domains grew weary.
translations.idiomatic: Though the frontier was pushed to Yuzhong and the Han Sea, wise ministers and brave generals exhausted every resource while the nomads slipped away and the empire grew weary.

sentences.zh: 于時賢哲，思造化之至理，推生民之習業。

translations.literal: Then worthy sages pondered the utmost principle of creation and transformation and inferred the customary occupations of the living people.
translations.idiomatic: Sages then pondered the laws of nature and the ways of different peoples.

sentences.zh: 量夫中夏粒食邑居之民、蠶衣儒步之士，荒表茹毛飲血之類、鳥宿禽居之徒，親校短長，因宜防制。

translations.literal: They measured the grain-eating, settled folk of the central domains and the silk-clad, Confucian-stepping gentlemen against the raw-flesh, blood-drinking kinds beyond the wastes and those who lodge with birds and dwell like beasts, personally comparing strengths and weaknesses and adapting defenses accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: They compared the settled, grain-farming people of the central realms with the raw-flesh nomads beyond the frontier and devised defenses suited to each.

sentences.zh: 知城郭之固，暫勞永逸。

translations.literal: They knew that the solidity of walled cities brings brief toil and lasting ease.
translations.idiomatic: They knew that walled cities bring brief toil and lasting security.

sentences.zh: 自皇魏統極，都於平城，威震天下，德籠宇宙。

translations.literal: Since the august Wei unified the pole and established its capital at Pingcheng, its might shook the realm and its virtue enveloped the cosmos.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Wei unified the realm and made Pingcheng its capital, its might shook the world.

sentences.zh: 今定鼎成周，去北遙遠。

translations.literal: Now the tripod is fixed at Zhou's completion and the north lies far away.
translations.idiomatic: Now the capital stands at Luoyang, far from the north.

sentences.zh: 代表諸蕃北固，高車外叛，尋遭旱儉，戎馬甲兵，十分闕八。

translations.literal: The Dai region and the various frontier peoples were secured in the north, yet the Gaoche rebelled outside; soon drought and famine followed, and of war horses and armor eight-tenths were lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Though the north was secured, the Gaoche rebelled abroad; drought and famine followed, and eight-tenths of horses and arms were gone.

sentences.zh: 去歲復鎮陰山，庶事蕩盡，遣尚書郎中韓貞、宋世量等檢行要險，防遏形便。

translations.literal: Last year the Yin Mountains were garrisoned again and all affairs were swept away; Attendant Gentleman Han Zhen, Song Shiliang, and others were sent to inspect vital passes and block according to terrain.
translations.idiomatic: Last year's Yin Mountain campaign exhausted everything. Han Zhen, Song Shiliang, and others were sent to survey the passes and plan defenses.

sentences.zh: 謂準舊鎮東西相望，令形勢相接，築城置戍，分兵要害，勸農積粟，警急之日，隨便翦討。

translations.literal: They proposed aligning with old garrisons facing east and west, making dispositions connect, building forts and setting posts, dividing troops at vital points, encouraging farming and storing grain—on days of alarm, cutting down the enemy as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed linking the old garrisons east and west, building forts and posts, garrisoning vital points, encouraging farming and storing grain, so that on alarm troops could strike at will.

sentences.zh: 如此則威形增廣，兵勢亦盛。

translations.literal: Thus prestige and form would broaden and military momentum also flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Thus our prestige would grow and our military strength increase.

sentences.zh: 且北方沙漠，夏乏水草，時有小泉，不濟大眾。

translations.literal: Moreover, the northern desert lacks water and grass in summer; occasional small springs cannot sustain great hosts.
translations.idiomatic: The northern desert lacks water and grass in summer; small springs cannot sustain large armies.

sentences.zh: 脫有非意，要待秋冬，因雲而動。

translations.literal: If they have other intentions, they must wait for autumn and winter and move with the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: If they mean mischief, they must wait until autumn and winter.

sentences.zh: 若至冬日，冰沙凝厲，遊騎之寇，終不敢攻城，亦不敢越城南出，如此北方無憂矣。」

translations.literal: When winter comes, ice and sand freeze hard; roaming cavalry raiders will not dare attack cities nor dare cross south of the walls—thus the north will be without worry."
translations.idiomatic: In winter, when ice binds the sand, roaming cavalry will not dare attack our cities or cross south of the walls—the north will be secure."

sentences.zh: 世宗從之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong accepted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 今北鎮諸戍東西九城是也。

translations.literal: The nine cities east and west of the northern garrisons today are this.
translations.idiomatic: These are the nine frontier cities east and west of the northern garrisons today.

sentences.zh: 遷驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand general of agile cavalry.

sentences.zh: 時武興氐王楊紹先叔集起反叛，詔懷使持節、侍中、都督平氐諸軍事以討之，須有興廢，任從權計。

translations.literal: At the time the Di king Yang Shaoxian's uncle Jiqi rebelled; an edict ordered Huai as envoy bearing the staff, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Supervisor of Military Affairs for Pacifying the Di to suppress him—where rise and abolition were needed, follow expedient stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: When the Di king Yang Shaoxian's uncle Jiqi rebelled, Huai was sent as envoy with credentials and attendant-in-ordinary to suppress him, with full discretion to act as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 其邢巒、李煥並禀節度。

translations.literal: Xing Luan and Li Huan both received his command.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Luan and Li Huan both served under his command.

sentences.zh: 三年六月卒，年六十三。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year he died, age sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth month of the third year, aged sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 詔給東園祕器、朝服一具、衣一襲、錢二十萬、布七百匹、蠟三百斤，贈司徒、冀州刺史。
