translations.literal: An edict granted eastern garden secret vessels, one set of court robes, one suit of clothes, two hundred thousand cash, seven hundred bolts of cloth, three hundred jin of wax; posthumously he was given Duke of the Masses and Inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted secret burial vessels, court robes, a suit of clothes, two hundred thousand cash, seven hundred bolts of cloth, and three hundred jin of wax, and was posthumously made duke of the masses and inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 兼吏部尚書盧昶奏：「太常寺議諡曰，懷體尚寬柔，器操平正，依諡法，柔直考終曰『靖』，宜諡靖公。

translations.literal: Concurrent Director of the Ministry of Personnel Lu Chang memorialized: "The Court of Imperial Sacrifices deliberated the posthumous title, saying Huai's substance valued breadth and gentleness, his capacity and conduct were level and correct; by posthumous law, gentle and upright to the end is 'Jing'—he should be posthumously titled Duke Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chang of the ministry of personnel reported that the court of imperial sacrifices proposed the posthumous title Jing, meaning gentle and upright to the end.

sentences.zh: 司徒府議，懷作牧陝西，民餘惠化，入總端貳，朝列歸仁，依諡法，布德執義曰『穆』，宜諡穆公。

translations.literal: The Secretariat of the Duke of the Masses deliberated that Huai as shepherd of Shaanxi left surplus benevolent transformation; entering to head the second rank, the court ranks returned to benevolence; by posthumous law, spreading virtue and holding to righteousness is 'Mu'—he should be posthumously titled Duke Mu.
translations.idiomatic: The secretariat of the duke of the masses proposed Mu, for spreading virtue and upholding righteousness.

sentences.zh: 二諡不同。」

translations.literal: The two posthumous titles differed."
translations.idiomatic: The two proposals differed.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「府、寺所執，並不克允，愛民好與曰『惠』，可諡惠公。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "What the secretariat and the sacrifices court hold is not fully fitting; loving the people and delighting in giving is 'Hui'—he may be posthumously titled Duke Hui."
translations.idiomatic: The edict ruled: "Neither proposal fully fits. Loving the people and delighting in generosity is Hui—he shall be posthumously titled Duke Hui."

sentences.zh: 懷性寬容簡約，不好煩碎，恒語人曰：「為貴人，理世務當舉綱維，何必須太子細也。

translations.literal: Huai was by nature tolerant, simple, and sparing, disliking trivial detail; he constantly told people: "As a noble man governing worldly affairs one should raise the net's cords—why must one be as fine as a prince's threads?
translations.idiomatic: Huai was tolerant and unpretentious, disliking petty detail. He often said, "A nobleman governing affairs should grasp the main lines—why fuss over every thread?

sentences.zh: 譬如為屋，但外望高顯，楹棟平正，基壁完牢，風雨不入，足矣。

translations.literal: It is like building a house: only that outwardly it looks high and prominent, pillars and beams are level and correct, foundation and walls complete and solid, wind and rain do not enter—that is enough.
translations.idiomatic: Building a house needs only a lofty appearance, straight pillars and beams, solid walls, and shelter from wind and rain—that is enough.

sentences.zh: 斧斤不平，斲削不密，非屋之病也。」

translations.literal: Axes and adzes not level, carving and paring not tight—these are not the house's illness."
translations.idiomatic: Rough axes and uneven carving are not the house's fault."

sentences.zh: 又性不飲酒而喜以飲人，好接賓友，雅善音律，雖在白首，至宴居之暇，常自操絲竹。

translations.literal: Further, by nature he did not drink but delighted in making others drink; he loved receiving guests and friends, was elegantly skilled in music; though white-haired, in leisure at banquets he often himself played string and bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: He did not drink himself but loved to host others; he welcomed guests and was skilled in music—even in old age he would play string and bamboo instruments at leisure.

sentences.zh: 懷有七子。

translations.literal: Huai had seven sons.
translations.idiomatic: Huai had seven sons.

sentences.zh: 長子規，字靈度。

translations.literal: His eldest son Gui, style Lingdu.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Gui, courtesy name Lingdu.

sentences.zh: 中書學生、羽林監，襲爵。

translations.literal: Student of the Secretariat, Supervisor of the Feathered Forest, inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: He was a student of the secretariat and supervisor of the feathered forest, and inherited his father's title.

sentences.zh: 年三十三卒。

translations.literal: He died at age thirty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at thirty-three.

sentences.zh: 子肅，襲。

translations.literal: His son Su succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Su inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子紹，襲。

translations.literal: His son Shao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shao inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 景明初，詔復王爵，[9]尋除隴西郡開國公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingming an edict restored the princely title;[9] soon he was appointed Duke of Longxi commandery with a state fief.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jingming his princely title was restored;[9] soon he was made Duke of Longxi with a state fief.

sentences.zh: 卒於光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He died as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 贈度支尚書、冀州刺史，諡曰文。

translations.literal: Posthumously given Director of the Revenue Section, Inspector of Jizhou; posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made director of the revenue section and inspector of Jizhou, with the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 子文遠，襲。

translations.literal: His son Wenyuan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wenyuan inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, by precedent he was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication his rank was reduced by precedent.

sentences.zh: 規弟榮，字靈並。

translations.literal: Gui's younger brother Rong, style Lingbing.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's younger brother Rong, courtesy name Lingbing.

sentences.zh: 年三十二，卒於司徒掾，贈光州刺史。

translations.literal: At age thirty-two he died as Secretariat Aide to the Duke of the Masses; posthumously given Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died at thirty-two while serving as secretariat aide to the duke of the masses and was posthumously made inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 榮弟徽，字靈祚。

translations.literal: Rong's younger brother Hui, style Lingzuo.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's younger brother Hui, courtesy name Lingzuo.

sentences.zh: 年二十八，卒於直閤將軍，特贈洛州刺史，諡曰質。

translations.literal: At age twenty-eight he died as General of the Direct Gate; specially posthumously given Inspector of Luozhou; posthumous title Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: He died at twenty-eight as general of the direct gate and was specially posthumously made inspector of Luozhou, with the posthumous title Zhi.

sentences.zh: 徽弟玄諒，出後懷弟奐。

translations.literal: Hui's younger brother Xuanliang was given in succession to Huai's younger brother Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's younger brother Xuanliang was adopted as heir to Huai's younger brother Huan.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈代郡太守。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously given Administrator of Dai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made administrator of Dai commandery.

sentences.zh: 玄諒弟子雍，字靈和。

translations.literal: Xuanliang's younger brother's son Yong, style Linghe.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanliang's nephew Yong, courtesy name Linghe.

sentences.zh: 少好文雅，篤志於學，推誠待士，士多歸之。

translations.literal: In youth he loved refinement and elegance, devoted his will to learning, extended sincerity in treating gentlemen, and many gentlemen rallied to him.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning and treated scholars with sincerity; many gathered to him.

sentences.zh: 自祕書郎，除太子舍人、涼州中正。

translations.literal: From Secretary he was appointed Household Attendant to the Heir Apparent and Chief Rectifier of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: From secretary he was made household attendant to the heir apparent and chief rectifier of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 肅宗踐阼，以宮臣例轉奉車都尉，遷司徒屬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong ascended the throne, by precedent for palace ministers he was transferred to Commandant of the Carriage for the Imperial Procession, then promoted to Secretariat Aide under the Duke of the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong ascended the throne he was transferred by precedent to commandant of the imperial procession, then to secretariat aide under the duke of the masses.

sentences.zh: 轉太中大夫、司徒司馬。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Master of Palace Counsel and Secretariat Marshal under the Duke of the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand master of palace counsel and secretariat marshal.

sentences.zh: 除恒農太守，遷夏州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Administrator of Hengnong, then transferred to Inspector of Xiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made administrator of Hengnong, then inspector of Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 時沃野鎮人破落汗拔陵首為反亂，所在蜂起，統萬逆胡，與相應接。

translations.literal: At the time the people of Woye garrison, Poluohan Baling, were first to rebel; everywhere they swarmed up, and the rebellious Hu of Tongwan responded in concert.
translations.idiomatic: When Poluohan Baling of Woye garrison first rebelled, uprisings erupted everywhere, and the rebels of Tongwan joined them.

sentences.zh: 子雍嬰城自守，城中糧盡，煮馬皮而食之。

translations.literal: Ziyong closed the city and held it; grain in the city was exhausted and they boiled horse hides to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyong held the city under siege until grain ran out and the defenders boiled horse hides to eat.

sentences.zh: 子雍善綏撫，得士心，人人戮力，無有離貳。

translations.literal: Ziyong was skilled in comforting and soothing, winning the hearts of his men; every man exerted strength and none turned away.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyong won his men's hearts through kindness; all fought as one without dissent.

sentences.zh: 以飢饉轉切，欲自出求糧，留子延伯據守。

translations.literal: As famine grew acute, he wished to go out himself to seek grain and leave his son Yanbo to hold the defense.
translations.idiomatic: As famine grew desperate he resolved to go out for grain himself and leave his son Yanbo to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 僚屬僉云：「今天下分析，寇賊萬重，四方音信，莫不斷絕，俄頃之間，變在不意，何宜父子如此分張？

translations.literal: His staff all said: "Now the realm is divided, bandits and enemies in myriad layers, news from the four directions all cut off—in a moment change may come unawares; how is it fitting for father and son to separate thus?
translations.idiomatic: His staff objected: "The realm is divided, enemies swarm on every side, and all communication is cut. Disaster may strike at any moment—how can father and son separate?

sentences.zh: 未若棄城俱去，更展規略。」

translations.literal: Better to abandon the city and leave together, then unfold strategy anew."
translations.idiomatic: Better to abandon the city together and plan anew."

sentences.zh: 子雍泣而謂眾曰：「吾世荷國恩，早受藩寄，此是吾死地，更欲何求！

translations.literal: Ziyong wept and told the assembly: "Our house has long borne the state's grace; early I received frontier trust—this is my ground to die; what more do I seek!
translations.idiomatic: Ziyong wept and told them, "My family has long served the state. This frontier post is my charge and my grave—what more could I want?

sentences.zh: 然守禦以來，歲月不淺，所患乏糧，不得制勝。

translations.literal: Yet since defense began the months are not shallow; what we suffer is lack of grain and cannot achieve victory.
translations.idiomatic: We have held the city long, but without grain we cannot win.

sentences.zh: 吾今向東州，得數月之食，還與諸人保全必矣。」

translations.literal: I now go to the eastern provinces; obtaining several months' food, I will return and with you all preservation is certain."
translations.idiomatic: I will go east for supplies. When I return with food for several months, we shall surely hold the city."

sentences.zh: 遂自率羸弱，向東夏運糧。

translations.literal: Thereupon he himself led the weak and went east to the Xia regions to transport grain.
translations.idiomatic: He then led a small force east to bring back grain.

sentences.zh: 延伯與將士送出城外，哭而拜辭，三軍莫不嗚咽。

translations.literal: Yanbo with officers and soldiers escorted him outside the walls, weeping and bowing farewell; the whole army none without sobbing.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo and the garrison escorted him beyond the walls, weeping as they took leave; the whole army sobbed.

sentences.zh: 子雍行數日，為朔方胡帥曹阿各拔所邀，力屈見執。

translations.literal: After several days on the road Ziyong was intercepted by the Shuo-fang Hu chieftain Cao Ageba; strength failed and he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: After several days he was intercepted by the Shuo-fang Hu chieftain Cao Ageba and captured.

sentences.zh: 子雍乃密遣人齎書，間行與城中文武云：「大軍在近，努力圍守，必令諸人福流苗裔。」

translations.literal: Ziyong then secretly sent a man bearing a letter by hidden route to the civil and military men in the city, saying: "The great army is near—strive to hold the siege; I will surely make your blessings flow to your descendants."
translations.idiomatic: Ziyong secretly sent a letter into the city: "Relief is near. Hold fast, and your descendants shall know blessing."

sentences.zh: 又敕延伯令共固守。

translations.literal: He also ordered Yanbo to hold firm together.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Yanbo to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 子雍雖被囚執，雅為胡人所敬，常以民禮事之。

translations.literal: Though Ziyong was imprisoned, the Hu by refinement respected him and constantly treated him with the rites due to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Though captive, he won the Hu's respect and was treated with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 子雍為陳安危禍福之理，勸阿各拔令降，阿各拔將從之，未果而死。

translations.literal: Ziyong set forth the principles of safety and danger, fortune and disaster, urging Ageba to submit; Ageba was about to consent but died before it was accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: He urged Ageba to submit by explaining the logic of safety and ruin. Ageba was about to agree when he died.

sentences.zh: 拔弟桑生代總部眾，竟隨子雍降。

translations.literal: Ba's younger brother Sangsheng succeeded in commanding the tribal host and in the end followed Ziyong in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Ageba's brother Sangsheng took command and eventually submitted with Ziyong.

sentences.zh: 時北海王顥為大行臺，子雍具陳賊可滅之狀。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Beihai, Hao, was Grand Mobile Secretariat; Ziyong fully stated how the bandits could be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Beihai Hao was then grand mobile secretariat; Ziyong explained fully how the rebels could be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 顥給子雍兵馬，令其先行。

translations.literal: Hao gave Ziyong troops and horses and ordered him to go ahead.
translations.idiomatic: Hao gave him troops and ordered him to advance first.

sentences.zh: 時東夏合境反叛，所在屯結。

translations.literal: At the time eastern Xia in the whole territory rebelled; everywhere they gathered in camps.
translations.idiomatic: The whole eastern region had rebelled and rebels gathered everywhere.

sentences.zh: 子雍轉鬬而前，九旬之中凡數十戰，仍平東夏，徵稅租粟，運於統萬。

translations.literal: Ziyong fought turning forward; in ninety days there were several tens of battles; he then pacified eastern Xia, levied rent grain, and transported it to Tongwan.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyong fought his way forward, engaging in dozens of battles over ninety days, pacified eastern Xia, levied grain, and shipped it to Tongwan.

sentences.zh: 於是二夏漸寧。

translations.literal: Thereupon the two Xia regions gradually grew calm.
translations.idiomatic: The two Xia regions were gradually pacified.

sentences.zh: 及蕭寶夤等為賊所敗，賊帥宿勤明達遣息阿非率眾邀路。

translations.literal: When Xiao Baoyin and others were defeated by bandits, the bandit chief Suqin Mingda sent his son Afei leading hosts to block the road.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Baoyin and others were defeated, the rebel chief Suqin Mingda sent his son Afei to block the road.

sentences.zh: 華州、白水被圍逼，關右騷擾，咫尺不通。

translations.literal: Huazhou and Baishui were besieged and pressed; west of the passes was in turmoil and within a foot's reach nothing passed.
translations.idiomatic: Huazhou and Baishui were besieged; the region west of the passes was in turmoil and communications were cut.

sentences.zh: 時子雍新平黑城，遂率士馬并夏州募義之民，攜家席卷，鼓行南出。

translations.literal: At the time Ziyong had newly pacified Heicheng; he then led soldiers and horses together with the volunteer people of Xiazhou, families rolled up in mats, beating drums marching south.
translations.idiomatic: Having just pacified Heicheng, Ziyong led his troops and Xiazhou volunteers south with their families, marching to the drum.

sentences.zh: 賊帥康維摩擁率羌胡守鋸谷，斷[嬰瓦]棠橋，子雍與交戰，大破之，生禽維摩。

translations.literal: The bandit chief Kang Weimo gathered and led Qiang and Hu to hold Jug Valley, cutting the Yingtang Bridge; Ziyong battled them, inflicted a great defeat, and captured Weimo alive.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Kang Weimo held Jug Valley with Qiang and Hu forces and cut the Yingtang Bridge. Ziyong attacked, routed them, and captured Weimo alive.

sentences.zh: 又攻賊帥契官斤於楊氏堡，破之。

translations.literal: He again attacked the bandit chief Qiguanjin at Yang's Fort and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He also defeated the rebel Qiguanjin at Yang's Fort.

sentences.zh: 子雍出自西夏，漸至於東，轉戰千里，至是，朝廷始得其委問。

translations.literal: Ziyong came out from western Xia and gradually reached the east, fighting turning over a thousand li—only then did the court first receive his detailed reports.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting from western Xia eastward over a thousand li, he at last sent detailed reports to the court.

sentences.zh: 除散騎常侍、使持節、假撫軍將軍、都督、兼行臺尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed Regular Attendant at the Palace Secretariat, envoy bearing the staff, acting General Who Pacifies the Army, Supervisor, and concurrent Mobile Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was made regular attendant at the palace secretariat, envoy with credentials, acting general who pacifies the army, supervisor, and concurrent mobile secretariat director.

sentences.zh: 復破賊帥紇單步胡提於曲沃堡。

translations.literal: He again defeated the bandit chief Hedan Buhuti at Quwo Fort.
translations.idiomatic: He again defeated the rebel chief Hedan Buhuti at Quwo Fort.

sentences.zh: 肅宗璽書勞勉之。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong sent an imperial sealed letter to commend and encourage him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong sent an imperial letter of commendation.

sentences.zh: 子雍在白水郡復破阿非軍，多所斬獲。

translations.literal: At Baishui commandery Ziyong again defeated Afei's army and beheaded and captured many.
translations.idiomatic: At Baishui he again routed Afei's force and took many heads and captives.

sentences.zh: 詔遣侍中、尚書令、城陽王徽於潼關宣旨慰勞。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Chengyang Yuan Hui to Tong Pass to proclaim the imperial will and offer condolences and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Masters of Writing Prince of Chengyang Yuan Hui to Tong Pass to convey the imperial message and offer encouragement.

sentences.zh: 除中軍將軍、金紫光祿大夫、給事黃門侍郎，封樂平縣開國公，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of the Central Army, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Girdle, Attendant at the Yellow Gate, and enfeoffed as Duke of Leping with founding fief, fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general of the central army, grand master of splendid happiness with golden seal and purple girdle, attendant at the yellow gate, and duke of Leping with a founding fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 還洛，以葛榮久逼信都，詔假子雍征北將軍，為北討都督。

translations.literal: Returning to Luoyang, because Ge Rong had long pressed Xindu, an edict made Ziyong acting General Who Pacifies the North and Northern Campaign Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Luoyang, with Ge Rong long besieging Xindu, an edict made Ziyong acting general who pacifies the north and northern campaign commander.

sentences.zh: 時相州刺史安樂王鑒據鄴反，敕子雍與都督李神軌先討之。

translations.literal: At the time Xiangzhou Inspector Prince of Anle Yuan Jian held Ye in rebellion; an order directed Ziyong and Commissioner Li Shengui to attack him first.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Anle Yuan Jian, inspector of Xiangzhou, held Ye in revolt; Ziyong and Commissioner Li Shengui were ordered to crush him first.

sentences.zh: 子雍行達湯陰，鑒遣弟斌之夜襲子雍軍，不克，奔敗而返。

translations.literal: Ziyong on the march reached Tangyin; Jian sent his younger brother Bin to night-assault Ziyong's army, failed, fled in defeat, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyong reached Tangyin; Jian sent his brother Bin to raid the camp by night, failed, and fled back in defeat.

sentences.zh: 子雍乘機繼進，徑圍鄴城，與裴衍、神軌等攻鑒，平之。

translations.literal: Ziyong seized the opportunity to press on, directly besieged Ye city, and with Pei Yan, Shengui, and others attacked Jian and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyong pressed on, besieged Ye, and with Pei Yan and Shengui defeated Jian and pacified the city.

sentences.zh: 改封陽平縣開國公，增邑千五百戶，進號鎮東將軍。

translations.literal: His fief was changed to Duke of Yangping with founding fief, household fief increased by one thousand five hundred, and he was promoted to General Who Guards the East.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was changed to duke of Yangping with a founding title, his household fief was increased by fifteen hundred, and he was promoted to general who guards the east.

sentences.zh: 遂與裴衍發鄴以討葛榮，而信都城陷。

translations.literal: He then with Pei Yan marched from Ye against Ge Rong, but Xindu city fell.
translations.idiomatic: He then left Ye with Pei Yan against Ge Rong, but Xindu fell.

sentences.zh: 除子雍冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Ziyong was appointed Jizhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyong was made inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 餘官如故。

translations.literal: His other offices remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: His other offices remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 子雍以冀州不守，上書曰：「賊中甚飢，專仰野掠。

translations.literal: Ziyong, because Jizhou could not be held, submitted a memorial saying, "The bandits are greatly famished and rely solely on raiding the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to hold Jizhou, Ziyong memorialized: "The rebels are starving and live only by raiding the countryside.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷足食，兵卒飽暖。

translations.literal: Now the court has ample food and the soldiers are fed and warm.
translations.idiomatic: The court has ample provisions and the troops are fed and warm.

sentences.zh: 高壁深壘，勿與爭鋒，彼求戰則不得，野掠無所獲，不盈數旬，可坐制凶醜。」

translations.literal: Build high walls and deep ramparts and do not contend at the spearpoint; when they seek battle they cannot have it, and raiding yields nothing—in less than several ten-day periods we can control the vicious rebels while seated."
translations.idiomatic: Raise high walls and deep ramparts and refuse battle; denied a fight and unable to raid for food, within weeks we can subdue these villains without stirring.

sentences.zh: 時裴衍復表求行，詔子雍與衍速進。

translations.literal: At the time Pei Yan again memorialized requesting to march; an edict ordered Ziyong and Yan to advance swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: At that point Pei Yan again asked to march, and an edict ordered Ziyong and Yan to advance at once.

sentences.zh: 子雍重表固請，如謂不可，乞令裴衍獨行。

translations.literal: Ziyong repeatedly memorialized and firmly requested that if the plan was deemed unfeasible, Pei Yan be allowed to march alone.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyong memorialized again and firmly asked that, if the plan was rejected, Pei Yan be allowed to march alone.

sentences.zh: 若不賜解，求停裴衍。

translations.literal: If release was not granted, he begged to halt Pei Yan.
translations.idiomatic: If he was not relieved of duty, he asked that Pei Yan be stopped.

sentences.zh: 苟逼同行，[10]取敗旦夕。

translations.literal: If forced to march together, [10] defeat would come within days.
translations.idiomatic: If forced to march together, [10] defeat would come within days.

sentences.zh: 詔不聽，遂與衍俱進。

translations.literal: The edict was not heeded, and he then advanced together with Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused; he advanced together with Yan.

sentences.zh: 至陽平郡東北漳曲，榮率賊十萬來逼官軍。

translations.literal: Reaching Zhangqu northeast of Yangping commandery, Rong led a hundred thousand bandits to press the government army.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhangqu northeast of Yangping commandery, Rong led a hundred thousand rebels against the government army.

sentences.zh: 子雍戰敗被害，年四十。

translations.literal: Ziyong was defeated in battle and killed; he was forty.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyong was defeated and killed; he was forty.

sentences.zh: 朝野痛惜之。

translations.literal: Court and countryside grieved for him.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country mourned him.

sentences.zh: 贈車騎大將軍、儀同三司、雍州刺史，公如故。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted General of Chariots and Cavalry, Honorary Three Departments, and Yongzhou Inspector; his ducal rank remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made general of chariots and cavalry, granted honorary three departments rank, and named inspector of Yongzhou; his ducal title remained.

sentences.zh: 永安中，重贈司空，諡曰莊穆。

translations.literal: In the Yong'an era he was again posthumously granted Minister of Works, posthumous title Zhuangmu.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yong'an era he was again posthumously made minister of works, with the posthumous name Solemn.

sentences.zh: 長子延伯，出後從伯。

translations.literal: The eldest son Yanbo was given in succession to a paternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Yanbo was adopted by a paternal uncle.

sentences.zh: 次子士則，早亡。

translations.literal: The second son Shize died early.
translations.idiomatic: The second son Shize died young.

sentences.zh: 士則弟士正、士規，並坐事死。

translations.literal: Shize's younger brothers Shizheng and Shigui both died for their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Shize's brothers Shizheng and Shigui both died for crimes.

sentences.zh: 次楷，字士質，小字那延，襲。

translations.literal: Next Kai, styled Shizhi, childhood name Nayan, inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Kai, styled Shizhi, childhood name Nayan, who inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 武定中，齊文襄王府參軍，齊受禪，例降。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era he was a staff officer in the princely establishment of Prince Wenxiang of Qi; when Qi received the abdication, his rank was reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wuding era he was a staff officer in the household of Prince Wenxiang of Qi; when Qi took the throne, his rank was reduced by precedent.

sentences.zh: 延伯，初為司空參軍事。

translations.literal: Yanbo initially served as staff officer under the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo first served as staff officer under the minister of works.

sentences.zh: 時南秦民吳富反叛，詔以河間王琛為都督，延伯叔父子恭為軍司。

translations.literal: At the time the commoner Wu Fu of southern Qin rebelled; an edict appointed Prince of Hejian Yuan Chen as commissioner and Yanbo's uncle's son Zigong as army secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When the commoner Wu Fu of southern Qin rebelled, Prince of Hejian Yuan Chen was made commissioner and Yanbo's cousin Zigong army secretary.

sentences.zh: 延伯為統軍，隨子恭西討，戰必先鋒。

translations.literal: Yanbo was army commander; following Zigong west to attack, in battle he always took the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo was army commander; marching west with Zigong, he always led the vanguard in battle.

sentences.zh: 子恭見其年幼，常訶制之而不能禁。

translations.literal: Zigong, seeing him young, often scolded and restrained him but could not stop him.
translations.idiomatic: Zigong, finding him too young, often scolded and restrained him but could not stop him.

sentences.zh: 子雍在夏州，表乞兵援，詔延伯率羽林一千人赴之，城鬬野戰，勇冠三軍。

translations.literal: Ziyong at Xiazhou memorialized begging military aid; an edict ordered Yanbo to lead one thousand imperial guards to go; in siege and field battle his valor topped the three armies.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiazhou Ziyong asked for reinforcements; Yanbo was ordered to lead a thousand imperial guards to his aid, and in siege and field battle his courage topped the army.

sentences.zh: 子雍之向東夏，留延伯城守，付以後事。

translations.literal: When Ziyong set out for eastern Xia, he left Yanbo to hold the city and entrusted him with subsequent affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Ziyong marched into eastern Xia, he left Yanbo to hold the city and entrusted him with everything that followed.

sentences.zh: 延伯與兵士共分湯菜，防固城隍。

translations.literal: Yanbo shared thin soup and vegetables with the soldiers and fortified the city walls and moat.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo shared thin soup and vegetables with the troops and strengthened the walls and moat.

sentences.zh: 及子雍為胡所執，合城憂懼，延伯乃人人曉喻曰：「吾父吉凶不測，方寸焦爛，實難裁割。

translations.literal: When Ziyong was seized by the Hu, the whole city was anxious and fearful; Yanbo then addressed each man, explaining, "My father's fortune or misfortune is unknowable; my heart is scorched—it is truly hard to divide public and private.
translations.idiomatic: When Ziyong was captured by the Hu, the whole city was terrified; Yanbo addressed the men one by one: "My father's fate is unknown; my heart is torn—it is hard to choose between public duty and private grief.

sentences.zh: 但奉命守城，所為處重，若以私害公，誠孝並闕，諸君幸得此心，無虧所寄。」

translations.literal: Yet having received orders to hold the city, what is done stands in weight; if I let private feeling harm public duty, both loyalty and filial piety fail—gentlemen, I hope you share this heart and do not fall short of what is entrusted."
translations.idiomatic: But I am under orders to hold the city, and that duty weighs heavily; if private grief harms public service, both loyalty and filial piety fail. I hope you share this resolve and do not betray what has been entrusted to us.

sentences.zh: 於是眾感其義，莫不勵憤。

translations.literal: Thereupon the multitude were moved by his righteousness; none failed to steel their resolve.
translations.idiomatic: The men were moved by his stand and steeled themselves to fight.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞而嘉之。

translations.literal: The court heard and commended it.
translations.idiomatic: The court heard and praised him.

sentences.zh: 除龍驤將軍，行夏州事，封五城縣開國子，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of Agile Cavalry, acting Xiazhou affairs, and enfeoffed as Viscount of Wucheng with founding fief, fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general of agile cavalry, acting governor of Xiazhou, and viscount of Wucheng with a founding fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 卒能固守。

translations.literal: In the end he was able to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he held firm.

sentences.zh: 及後刺史至，延伯率領義眾還赴子雍，共平黑城。

translations.literal: When the later inspector arrived, Yanbo led volunteer forces back to join Ziyong and together pacified Heicheng.
translations.idiomatic: When the new inspector arrived, Yanbo led volunteer troops back to Ziyong and together they pacified Heicheng.

sentences.zh: 在[嬰瓦]棠橋戰，先鋒陷陳，身擒維摩。

translations.literal: In battle at Yingtang Bridge he led the vanguard into the enemy lines and personally captured Weimo.
translations.idiomatic: At Yingtang Bridge he led the vanguard into the enemy lines and captured Weimo himself.

sentences.zh: 及至白水，首摧阿非。

translations.literal: Reaching Baishui, he first crushed Afei.
translations.idiomatic: At Baishui he was first to defeat Afei.

sentences.zh: 隨子雍至都，進爵浮陽伯，增封百戶，為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Following Ziyong to the capital, he was advanced in rank to Baron of Fuyang, household fief increased by one hundred, and made Remonstrance and Review Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Following Ziyong to the capital, he was raised to baron of Fuyang, given a hundred additional households, and made remonstrance and review grand master.

sentences.zh: 假冠軍將軍、別將，隨子雍北討。

translations.literal: Acting General Who Establishes Victory and separate commander, he followed Ziyong on the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: As acting general who establishes victory and separate commander, he followed Ziyong on the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 與葛榮戰歿，時年二十四。

translations.literal: He died fighting Ge Rong; he was twenty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died fighting Ge Rong at the age of twenty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈持節、平北將軍、涼州刺史，開國如故。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted bearer of the staff, General Who Pacifies the North, and Liangzhou Inspector; his founding fief remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made bearer of the staff, general who pacifies the north, and inspector of Liangzhou; his founding title remained.

sentences.zh: 子孝孫，襲。

translations.literal: His son Xiaosun inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaosun inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, his rank was reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne, his rank was reduced by precedent.

sentences.zh: 子雍弟子恭，字靈順，聰惠好學。

translations.literal: Ziyong's younger brother's son Zigong, styled Lingshun, was intelligent and fond of learning.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyong's nephew Zigong, styled Lingshun, was clever and studious.

sentences.zh: 初辟司空參軍事。

translations.literal: He was initially recruited as staff officer under the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was first recruited as staff officer under the minister of works.

sentences.zh: 司徒祭酒、尚書北主客郎中，攝南主客事。

translations.literal: Director of Libations under the Minister of Education, Northern Host-Guest Gentleman in the Masters of Writing, and concurrently handling southern host-guest affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He became director of libations under the minister of education, northern host-guest gentleman in the masters of writing, and concurrently handled southern host-guest affairs.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍亡人許周自稱為衍給事黃門待郎，朝士翕然，咸共信待。

translations.literal: Xu Zhou, a defector from Xiao Yan, claimed to be Yan's Attendant at the Yellow Gate; court scholars stirred together and all trusted and received him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhou, a defector from Xiao Yan, claimed to be Yan's attendant at the yellow gate; court scholars flocked to him and all trusted him.

sentences.zh: 子恭奏曰：「徐州表投化人許團并其弟周等。

translations.literal: Zigong memorialized, saying, "Xuzhou reported surrendered subjects Xu Tuan and his younger brother Zhou and others.
translations.idiomatic: Zigong memorialized: "Xuzhou reported the surrender of Xu Tuan and his brother Zhou and others.

sentences.zh: 究其牒狀，周列云己蕭衍黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Examining their documents, Zhou listed himself as Xiao Yan's Yellow Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Examining their documents, Zhou listed himself as Xiao Yan's yellow gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 又稱心存山水，不好榮宦，屢曾辭讓，貽彼赫怒，遂被出為齊康郡。

translations.literal: He also claimed his heart lay in mountains and waters, that he disliked glory and office, repeatedly declined, provoked Yan's great anger, and was sent out as governor of Qikang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He also claimed to love mountains and streams, dislike rank and office, and to have declined repeatedly until Yan's wrath sent him out as governor of Qikang commandery.

sentences.zh: 因爾歸國，願畢志嵩嶺。

translations.literal: Thereupon he returned to our state, wishing to fulfill his aspiration on Song Peak.
translations.idiomatic: He then came to our state, wishing to fulfill his aspiration on Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 比加採訪，略無證明；

translations.literal: When investigation was added, there was scarcely any proof;
translations.idiomatic: Further inquiry found almost no proof;

sentences.zh: 尋其表狀，又復莫落。

translations.literal: Searching his memorials and documents, they were again sparse.
translations.idiomatic: and his memorials and records were again sparse.

sentences.zh: 案牒推理，實有所疑。

translations.literal: Examining documents and reasoning, there is indeed doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing the documents, I find real grounds for doubt.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 昔夷齊獨往，周王不屈其志；

translations.literal: Formerly Boyi and Shuqi went alone, and the Zhou king did not bend their will;
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Boyi and Shuqi went their own way, and the Zhou king did not bend their will;

sentences.zh: 伯況辭祿，漢帝因成其美。

translations.literal: Bo Tong declined salary, and the Han emperor thereby made his virtue complete.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Tong declined salary, and the Han emperor honored his choice.

sentences.zh: 斯實古先哲王，必有不臣之人者也。

translations.literal: This truly shows that the sage kings of old necessarily had men who would not serve as subjects.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that sage kings of old respected men who would not serve as ordinary subjects.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍雖復崎嶇江左，竊號一隅，至於處物，未甚悖禮。

translations.literal: Though Xiao Yan was rugged in the lands east of the river and usurped title in one corner, in dealing with people he was not greatly contrary to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xiao Yan held a corner of the land east of the river and usurped a title, in his dealings he was not greatly contrary to ritual.

sentences.zh: 豈有士辭榮祿而苟不聽之哉？

translations.literal: How could there be a scholar declining glory and salary whom he simply would not heed?
translations.idiomatic: Would he simply ignore a scholar who declined rank and salary?

sentences.zh: 推察情理，此則孟浪。

translations.literal: Weighing the circumstances and reasoning, this is rash.
translations.idiomatic: Weighing the circumstances, this claim is implausible.

sentences.zh: 假蕭衍昏狂，[11]不存雅道，逼士出郡，未為死急，何宜輕去生養之土，長辭父母之邦乎？

translations.literal: Even assuming Xiao Yan was muddled and mad, [11] did not preserve the elegant way, and forced a scholar out of his commandery—not a matter of life-or-death urgency—why should one lightly leave the land that nurtured one and forever bid farewell to one's parents' country?
translations.idiomatic: Even if Xiao Yan were mad, [11] abandoned propriety, and forced a scholar from his commandery, that is hardly a matter of life and death—why lightly abandon the land that nurtured you and forever leave your native country?

sentences.zh: 若言不好榮官，志願嵩嶺者，初屆之日，即應杖策尋山，負帙沿水，而乃廣尋知己，遍造執事，希榮之心已見，逃宦之志安在？

translations.literal: If he says he dislikes glorious office and aspires to Song Peak, on the day he first arrived he should have leaned on his staff to seek mountains and carried scrolls along the waters—yet instead he widely sought acquaintances and visited every office holder; desire for glory is already seen—where is the will to flee office?
translations.idiomatic: If he truly disliked rank and aspired to Mount Song, he should have taken staff and scrolls to the hills on his first day here; instead he sought patrons everywhere and visited every official—his hunger for glory is plain, and where is his wish to flee office?

sentences.zh: 昔梁鴻去鄉，終傭吳會；

translations.literal: Formerly Liang Hong left his district and finally hired himself out in Wu and Kuai;
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Liang Hong left his home and ended as a hired hand in Wu and Kuai;

sentences.zh: 逄萌浮海，遠客遼東。

translations.literal: Pang Meng crossed the sea and was a distant guest in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Meng crossed the sea and lived as a distant guest in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 並全志養性，逍遙而已，考之事實，何其懸哉？

translations.literal: Both fully preserved their will and nourished their nature, roaming freely—compared with the facts, how far apart!
translations.idiomatic: Both preserved their will and lived freely—compared with the facts, how far apart they are!

sentences.zh: 又其履歷清華，名位高達，計其家累，應在不輕。

translations.literal: Moreover his career was pure and splendid, his name and rank reached high; reckoning his household dependents, they should be no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover his career was distinguished and his rank high; his household dependents cannot have been few.

sentences.zh: 今者歸化，何其孤迥？

translations.literal: Now in surrender, how solitary and abrupt?
translations.idiomatic: Yet in coming over now, how solitary and abrupt he is!

sentences.zh: 設使當時怱遽，不得攜將，及其來後，家貲產業應見簿斂，尊卑口累亦當從法。

translations.literal: Suppose at the time he was in haste and could not bring them—after his arrival, household property should appear in registers for collection, and dependents high and low should likewise follow the law.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose he fled in haste and could not bring them—after his arrival, household property should be registered and taxed, and dependents of every rank should be accounted for by law.

sentences.zh: 而周兄弟怡然，嘗無憂戚。

translations.literal: Yet the Zhou brothers are at ease, entirely without worry or grief.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Zhou brothers are at ease, with no sign of worry or grief.

sentences.zh: 若無種族，理或可通，如有不坐，便應是衍故遣，非周投化。

translations.literal: If they have no clan, reason might permit it; if some were not brought, it should be that Yan deliberately sent them—not Zhou surrendering.
translations.idiomatic: If they have no kin, that might be explained; if some were left behind, it must be that Yan sent Zhou here deliberately rather than that Zhou came of his own accord.

sentences.zh: 推究二三，真偽難辨，請下徐揚二州密訪，必令獲實，不盈數旬，玉石可覩。」

translations.literal: Investigating two or three points, true and false are hard to distinguish; I beg that secret investigation be sent to Xu and Yang provinces, surely to obtain the truth—in less than several ten-day periods jade and stone can be seen."
translations.idiomatic: Pursue two or three of these points and truth and falsehood cannot easily be told apart; please order secret inquiry in Xu and Yang provinces, and within weeks the genuine and the false will be plain.

sentences.zh: 於是詔推訪，周果以罪歸闕，假稱職位，如子恭所疑。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered investigation; Zhou indeed returned to court under charge, having falsely claimed office, just as Zigong had suspected.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered investigation; Zhou was brought back under charge for falsely claiming rank, just as Zigong had suspected.

sentences.zh: 河州羌却鐵怱反，[12]殺害長吏，詔子恭持節為行臺，率諸將討之。

translations.literal: Hezhou Qiang Qie Tiecang rebelled, [12] killing senior officials; an edict ordered Zigong, bearer of the staff, as mobile commissioner, leading the generals to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Qie Tiecang of the Hezhou Qiang rebelled, [12] killing senior officials; Zigong was ordered as mobile commissioner with imperial credentials to lead the generals against him.

sentences.zh: 子恭嚴勒州郡及諸軍，不得犯民一物，輕與賊戰，然後示以威恩，兩旬間悉皆降款。

translations.literal: Zigong strictly commanded the prefectures, commanderies, and all armies not to violate a single thing belonging to the people, fought lightly with the bandits, and then showed both sternness and kindness; within twenty days all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zigong strictly forbade the prefectures, commanderies, and armies to harm the people in the least, fought the rebels cautiously, then showed both sternness and kindness; within twenty days all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉之。

translations.literal: The court commended him.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised him.

sentences.zh: 正光元年，為行臺左丞，巡行北邊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengguang he was Left Director of the Mobile Secretariat, touring the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengguang 1 he was left director of the mobile secretariat, touring the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 轉為起部郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Construction Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to gentleman of the construction bureau.

sentences.zh: 明堂、辟雍並未建就，子恭上書曰：「臣聞辟臺望氣，軌物之德既高；

translations.literal: The Bright Hall and Imperial Academy were not yet completed; Zigong submitted a memorial saying, "Your servant hears that the raised platform for observing qi—virtue that sets all things on track is already lofty;
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Hall and Imperial Academy were not yet finished; Zigong submitted a memorial: "I have heard that the raised platform for observing the qi of heaven shows virtue that orders all things;

sentences.zh: 方堂布政，範世之道斯遠。

translations.literal: the square hall for dispensing governance—the Way that models the world is thus far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: and the square hall for dispensing governance shows a Way that models the world.

sentences.zh: 是以書契之重，理冠於造化；

translations.literal: Therefore the weight of writing on bamboo and cord—its principle crowns creation;
translations.idiomatic: The weight of writing and record surpasses creation itself;

sentences.zh: 推尊之美，事絕於生民。

translations.literal: the beauty of exalting the honored—a matter beyond ordinary people.
translations.idiomatic: and the beauty of honoring the supreme stands above ordinary human affairs.

sentences.zh: 至如郊天饗帝，蓋以對越上靈；

translations.literal: As for sacrificing to Heaven in the suburbs and offering to the Emperor—it is to respond to and approach the supreme spirits;
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice to Heaven in the suburbs and offerings to the Lord on High respond to the supreme spirits;

sentences.zh: 宗祀配天，是用酬膺下土。

translations.literal: ancestral worship with Heaven as counterpart is to repay receiving charge over the lower realm.
translations.idiomatic: ancestral worship paired with Heaven repays the charge received over the realm below.

sentences.zh: 大孝莫之能加，嚴父以茲為大，乃皇王之休業，有國之盛典。

translations.literal: Greatest filial piety cannot be exceeded; revering the father takes this as greatest—it is the splendid enterprise of emperors and kings and the grand ceremony of those who possess a state.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing exceeds the greatest filial piety; reverence for the father is its crown—the splendid work of emperors and kings and the grand ceremony of any state.

sentences.zh: 竊惟皇魏居震統極，總宙馭宇，革制土中，垂式無外。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Great Wei, dwelling in the east, uniting the ultimate, governing the cosmos and steering the universe, changing institutions at the center of the land, extends models without limit.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Great Wei, rooted in the east and holding the ultimate pole, governs heaven and earth, reforms institutions at the center of the land, and sets a model for all beyond.

sentences.zh: 自北徂南，同卜維於洛食；

translations.literal: From north to south, together divined to establish at Luoyang's nourishment;
translations.idiomatic: From north to south it divined alike to establish itself at Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 定鼎遷民，均氣候於寒暑。

translations.literal: fixed the cauldrons and moved the people, equalizing climate between cold and heat.
translations.idiomatic: fixed the cauldrons, moved the people, and balanced the climates of cold and heat.

sentences.zh: 高祖所以始基，世宗於是恢構。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu thereby began the foundation; Emperor Shizong thus expanded the structure.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu laid the foundation; Emperor Shizong expanded the structure.

sentences.zh: 按功成作樂，治定制禮，乃訪遺文，修廢典，建明堂，立學校，興一代之茂矩，標千載之英規。

translations.literal: Examining the principle that when merit is complete music is made and when order is settled rites are fixed—thereupon sought lost texts, restored abolished canons, built the Bright Hall, established schools, raised a flourishing model for an age, and marked a heroic standard for a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: When merit is complete, music follows; when order is settled, rites are fixed—thereupon lost texts were sought, abolished canons restored, the Bright Hall built, schools established, a flourishing model raised for the age, and a standard set for a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 永平之中，始創雉構，基趾草昧，迄無成功。

translations.literal: During the Yongping era they first began the initial framework; the foundation site remained primeval and unformed, and in the end there was no success.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongping era construction was first begun, but the foundations lay still raw and unformed, and nothing was ever completed.

sentences.zh: 故尚書令、任城王臣澄按故司空臣沖所造明堂樣，并連表詔答、兩京模式，奏求營起。

translations.literal: The former Minister over the Masters of Writing, Prince of Rencheng, your subject Chen, examined the Bright Hall model made by the late Minister of Works, your subject Chong, together with the linked memorials, edict responses, and models of the two capitals, and memorialized requesting that construction be undertaken.
translations.idiomatic: The former minister over the masters of writing, Prince of Rencheng Chen, reviewed the Bright Hall model made by the late minister of works Chong, together with the related memorials, imperial replies, and models of the two capitals, and submitted a request to begin construction.

sentences.zh: 緣期發旨，即加葺繕。

translations.literal: When the deadline arrived and the decree was issued, repairs and construction were immediately added.
translations.idiomatic: When the appointed date came and the decree went out, work on repairs began at once.

sentences.zh: 侍中、領軍臣叉，總動作官，[13]宣贊授令。

translations.literal: The Minister of the Household and General of the Guard, your subject Cha, oversaw the construction officials, [13] proclaiming and conveying orders.
translations.idiomatic: The minister of the household and general of the guard, Cha, took overall charge of the construction officials, [13] issuing and relaying orders.

sentences.zh: 自茲厥後，方配兵人，或給一千，或與數百，進退節縮，曾無定準，欲望速了，理在難克。

translations.literal: From then on, when military men were assigned, sometimes a thousand were given, sometimes several hundred; advance and withdrawal were curtailed with no fixed standard—hoping for swift completion, reason says it was hard to achieve.
translations.idiomatic: After that, laborers were drawn from the army in batches of a thousand here, a few hundred there, increased or cut back without any fixed rule; to expect quick completion was, by any reckoning, impossible.

sentences.zh: 若使專役此功，長得營造，委成責辦，容有就期。

translations.literal: If dedicated laborers were assigned solely to this work, always able to build, with commission and responsibility for completion, there might be meeting the deadline.
translations.idiomatic: If men were assigned exclusively to this project, kept at the work without interruption, and held accountable until it was finished, the deadline might yet be met.

sentences.zh: 但所給之夫，本自寡少，諸處競借，動即千計。

translations.literal: But the laborers assigned were originally few to begin with; everywhere competed to borrow them, and movement immediately reached the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: But the men allotted were too few from the start, and every office competed to borrow them until thousands were pulled away at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 雖有繕作之名，終無就功之實。

translations.literal: Though there was a name for construction, in the end there was no reality of completed work.
translations.idiomatic: Construction existed in name only, and nothing was ever truly finished.

sentences.zh: 爽塏荒茫，淹積年載，結架崇構，指就無兆。

translations.literal: Bright and open yet desolate and boundless, accumulated over years; raising frames and lofty structures, aiming at completion showed no omen.
translations.idiomatic: The site lay bright and empty, desolate year after year; timber frames and towering structures rose, yet completion seemed nowhere in sight.

sentences.zh: 仍令肄冑之禮，掩仰而不進；

translations.literal: Still causing the rite of martial drill to be covered over and held back without advancing;
translations.idiomatic: The rite of martial drill remains suspended, covered over and unperformed;

sentences.zh: 養老之儀，寂寥而不返。

translations.literal: the ceremony of nurturing the aged, lonely and not returning.
translations.idiomatic: and the ceremony honoring the aged stands abandoned, with no sign of revival.

sentences.zh: 構厦止於尺土，為山頓於一匱，良可惜歟！

translations.literal: Building a great hall stops at one foot of earth; piling a mountain halts at one basket-load—how truly regrettable!
translations.idiomatic: A hall abandoned after a foot of earth is laid, a mountain left unfinished with one basket of soil still to go—what a waste!

sentences.zh: 愚謂召民經始，必有子來之歌；

translations.literal: I think that when the people are summoned to begin, there must be a song of 'the sons come';
translations.idiomatic: I believe that when the people are called to begin the work, there will be a song of willing labor;

sentences.zh: 興造勿亟，將致不日之美。

translations.literal: Do not hurry construction, and one will attain the beauty of 'not a day.'
translations.idiomatic: and if construction is not rushed, the beauty of swift completion will follow in its own time.

sentences.zh: 況本兵不多，兼之牽役，廢此與彼，循環無極。

translations.literal: Moreover the original troops are not many; adding forced labor, abandoning this for that, cycling without end.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the army is already small, and with conscript labor pulled now here, now there, the cycle never ends.

sentences.zh: 便是輟創禮之重，資不急之費，廢經國之功，供寺館之役，求之遠圖，不亦闕矣？

translations.literal: This is to halt the weight of founding rites, supply non-urgent expense, abandon state-founding merit, and supply temple and pavilion labor—seeking far-reaching plans, is this not a deficiency?
translations.idiomatic: To set aside the weight of founding rites, spend on what is not urgent, abandon work that sustains the state, and supply labor for temples and halls—can any far-sighted plan afford such neglect?

sentences.zh: 今諸寺大作，稍以粗舉，並可徹減，專事經綜，嚴勒工匠，務令克成。

translations.literal: Now the various temples are being built on a grand scale, somewhat roughly raised—all can be withdrawn and reduced, concentrating on the Bright Hall and Imperial Academy, strictly commanding the craftsmen, ensuring completion.
translations.idiomatic: The great temple projects now under way, even if only roughly begun, should all be cut back; concentrate on the Bright Hall and Imperial Academy, keep the craftsmen under strict command, and see the work through to completion.

sentences.zh: 使祖宗有薦配之期，蒼生覩禮樂之富。」

translations.literal: So that the ancestors have a date for offering sacrifice, and the common people behold the wealth of rites and music.
translations.idiomatic: Then the ancestors may receive their offerings on schedule, and the people may witness the full splendor of rites and music.

sentences.zh: 書奏，從之。

translations.literal: 」 The memorial was submitted and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted and accepted.

sentences.zh: 除冠軍將軍、中散大夫，又領治書侍御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Quells the Champions and Palace Attendant of the Central Staff, and also appointed Supervising Secretary Attendant of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general who quells the champions and palace attendant of the central staff, and also supervising secretary attendant of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 秦益氐反，詔子恭持節為都督、河間王琛軍司以討之。

translations.literal: The Qin and Yi Di rebelled; an edict ordered Zigong, bearer of the staff, as army secretary under the commissioner Prince of Hejian Chen to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qin and Yi Di rebelled, Zigong was ordered, with imperial credentials, to serve as army secretary under Prince of Hejian Chen and campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 事平，仍行南秦州事。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he still administered southern Qin province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign ended, he continued to administer southern Qin province.

sentences.zh: 及六鎮反，以子恭兼給事黃門郎，持節慰勞。

translations.literal: When the Six Garrisons rebelled, Zigong was additionally appointed Attendant of Affairs at the Yellow Gate, bearer of the staff to comfort and encourage.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Garrisons rose in revolt, Zigong was additionally made attendant of affairs at the yellow gate and sent with imperial credentials to comfort the troops.

sentences.zh: 還，拜河內太守，加後將軍，平絳蜀反。

translations.literal: On return he was appointed Administrator of Henei, promoted to Rear General, and pacified the Jiang and Shu rebels.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed administrator of Henei and promoted to rear general, and he pacified the Jiang and Shu rebels.

sentences.zh: 丹谷、清廉二路險澀不通，以子恭為當郡別將。

translations.literal: The Dangu and Qinglian routes were treacherous and blocked; Zigong was made separate commander for that commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Dangu and Qinglian passes were treacherous and impassable, and Zigong was made separate commander for the commandery.

sentences.zh: [14]俄而建興蜀復反，相與連勢，進子恭為持節、散騎常侍、假平北將軍、征建興都督，仍兼尚書行臺，與正平都督長孫稚合勢進討，大破之。

translations.literal: [14] Soon the Jianxing Shu rebelled again, linking forces; Zigong was promoted to bearer of the staff, Regular Attendant at the Capital Gate, Acting General Who Pacifies the North, Commissioner for Jianxing, still concurrently Masters of Writing mobile bureau, joined with Zhengping Commissioner Zhangsun Zhi's forces to advance and attack, and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: [14] Soon the Jianxing Shu rebelled again and joined forces; Zigong was promoted to bearer of the staff, regular attendant at the capital gate, acting general who pacifies the north, and commissioner for Jianxing, while still holding the masters of writing mobile bureau. He joined Zhengping commissioner Zhangsun Zhi, advanced together, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 正平賊帥范明遠與賊帥劉牙奴並面縛請降。

translations.literal: The Zhengping bandit chief Fan Mingyuan and the bandit chief Liu Yanu both bound themselves and requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhengping rebel leaders Fan Mingyuan and Liu Yanu both came forward bound and asked to surrender.

sentences.zh: 事平，除平南將軍、豫州刺史，尋加散騎常侍、撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Yuzhou; soon added Regular Attendant at the Capital Gate and General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign ended he was made general who pacifies the south and governor of Yuzhou, and soon afterward was also given regular attendant at the capital gate and general who pacifies the army.

sentences.zh: 武泰初，郢州刺史元願達以城降蕭衍，詔徵都督尉慶賓還京師，回眾隸子恭以討之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wutai, Yingzhou Governor Yuan Yuanda surrendered the city to Xiao Yan; an edict summoned Commissioner Wei Qingbin back to the capital and turned the masses over to Zigong to attack.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wutai era, Yingzhou governor Yuan Yuanda surrendered his city to Xiao Yan; Wei Qingbin was recalled to the capital, and his troops were placed under Zigong to mount the counterattack.

sentences.zh: 衍將夏侯夔率眾數萬來寇，遠近不安。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's general Xiahou Man led tens of thousands to invade; near and far were unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan's general Xiahou Man marched in with tens of thousands of men, and the region was thrown into alarm.

sentences.zh: 夔乘勢分兵，遂逼新蔡，自攻毛城。

translations.literal: Man seized the momentum to divide his troops, then pressed toward Xincai and himself attacked Maocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Man took advantage of the moment to split his forces, pressed toward Xincai, and himself attacked Maocheng.

sentences.zh: 子恭隨方應援，賊並破走。

translations.literal: Zigong responded according to each direction with relief; the bandits were all defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zigong sent relief wherever it was needed and drove the enemy back on every front.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍豫州刺史夏侯亶復遣四將，率眾三萬，入圍南頓，北攻陳項。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's Yuzhou Governor Xiahou Dan again sent four generals, leading thirty thousand men to besiege Nandun and attack north toward Chen and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan's Yuzhou governor Xiahou Dan sent four more generals with thirty thousand men to besiege Nandun and strike north toward Chen and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 子恭遣軍禦之，賊復奔退。

translations.literal: Zigong sent armies to resist them; the bandits again fled in retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Zigong sent troops against them, and the enemy fled once more.

sentences.zh: 加鎮南將軍，又兼尚書行臺。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General Who Guards the South and again concurrently held the Masters of Writing mobile bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general who guards the south and again held the masters of writing mobile bureau.

sentences.zh: 子恭勒眾渡淮，徙民於淮北，立郡縣，置戍而還。

translations.literal: Zigong led the masses across the Huai, moved the people north of the Huai, established prefectures and counties, set garrisons, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zigong crossed the Huai with his army, resettled the people north of the river, established prefectures and counties, posted garrisons, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍直閤將軍、軍主胡智達等八將，與其監軍閻次洪入寇，屯於州城東北四十餘里。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's Direct Attendant General and army commander Hu Zhida and eight other generals, with their supervising general Yan Cihong, invaded and encamped more than forty li northeast of the provincial city.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan's direct attendant general and army commander Hu Zhida, seven other generals, and their supervising general Yan Cihong invaded and encamped some forty li northeast of the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 子恭擊破之，斬智達，生擒次洪。

translations.literal: Zigong defeated them, beheaded Zhida, and captured Cihong alive.
translations.idiomatic: Zigong routed them, killed Zhida, and took Cihong alive.

sentences.zh: 元顥之入洛也，加子恭車騎將軍，子恭不敢拒之，而頻遣間使參莊帝動靜。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Zigong was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry; Zigong dared not refuse, but frequently sent secret envoys to observe Emperor Zhuang's movements.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Zigong was promoted to general of chariots and cavalry. He did not dare refuse, but he repeatedly sent secret envoys to report on Emperor Zhuang's movements.

sentences.zh: 未幾，顥敗，車駕還洛，進征南將軍、兼右僕射，假車騎將軍，後加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Before long Hao was defeated, the imperial carriage returned to Luoyang; Zigong was promoted to General Who Campaigns the South and concurrently Right Vice Director, Acting General of Chariots and Cavalry, and later added Regular Attendant at the Capital Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Hao was defeated and the emperor returned to Luoyang. Zigong was promoted to general who campaigns the south and right vice director, given acting rank as general of chariots and cavalry, and later made regular attendant at the capital gate.

sentences.zh: 板橋蠻文石活、石忌麤受蕭衍印節，扇誘黨類，據險寇竊。

translations.literal: The Banqiao barbarians Wen Shihuo and Wen Jicu received seals and credentials from Xiao Yan, incited their faction, held dangerous terrain, and raided.
translations.idiomatic: The Banqiao tribesmen Wen Shihuo and Wen Jicu accepted seals and credentials from Xiao Yan, stirred up their followers, seized the high ground, and launched raids.

sentences.zh: 子恭躬率將士，徑襲其柵，數日之中，殲殪略盡。

translations.literal: Zigong personally led officers and soldiers, directly attacked their palisade, and within several days nearly all were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Zigong led his officers and men in person, struck their stockade directly, and within days had all but wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 諸蠻款服，咸求輸稅。

translations.literal: All the barbarians submitted, all sought to deliver taxes.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes all submitted and asked to pay tribute.

sentences.zh: 徵拜右光祿大夫、給事黃門侍郎，仍本將軍。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Right Director of the Imperial Household and Attendant of Affairs at the Yellow Gate, still holding his original generalship.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court as right director of the imperial household and attendant of affairs at the yellow gate, while retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 錄其前後征討功，封臨潁縣開國侯，食邑六百戶，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Recording his previous and subsequent campaign merits, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of a chief district at Linying, fief of six hundred households, and added Regular Attendant at the Capital Gate.
translations.idiomatic: His earlier and later campaign achievements were recorded, and he was enfeoffed as marquis of a chief district at Linying with a fief of six hundred households and given regular attendant at the capital gate.

sentences.zh: 俄遷侍中。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Minister of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made minister of the household.

sentences.zh: 尒朱榮之死也，世隆、度律據斷河橋，詔子恭為都督以討之，出頓於大夏門北。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong died, Shilong and Dulü held and blocked the river bridge; an edict appointed Zigong as commissioner to attack them, and he went out and encamped north of Daxia Gate.
translations.idiomatic: After Erzhu Rong's death, Shilong and Dulü seized and blocked the river bridge. Zigong was ordered as commissioner to attack them and encamped north of Daxia Gate.

sentences.zh: 尋而太府卿李苗夜燒河橋，世隆退走，仍以子恭兼尚書僕射，為大行臺、大都督。

translations.literal: Soon Grand Steward Li Miao burned the river bridge by night; Shilong retreated and fled; Zigong was still made concurrently Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Great Mobile Bureau, and Grand Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Grand Steward Li Miao burned the bridge by night. Shilong withdrew, and Zigong was made vice director of the masters of writing, great mobile bureau, and grand commissioner.

sentences.zh: 尋遷衞將軍、假車騎將軍，率諸將於太行築壘以防之。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to General of the Guard and Acting General of Chariots and Cavalry, leading the generals to build fortifications at the Taihang Mountains to defend against them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made general of the guard and acting general of chariots and cavalry, and led the generals to build fortifications in the Taihang Mountains against the enemy.

sentences.zh: 既而尒朱兆率眾南出，子恭所部都督史仵龍、羊文義開柵降兆。

translations.literal: Before long Erzhu Zhao led the masses south; Zigong's subordinate commissioners Shi Wulong and Yang Wenyi opened the palisade gates and surrendered to Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Erzhu Zhao marched south. Two of Zigong's subordinate commissioners, Shi Wulong and Yang Wenyi, opened the gates and surrendered to Zhao.

sentences.zh: 子恭退走，為兆所破。

translations.literal: Zigong retreated and fled, and was defeated by Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zigong fell back and was routed by Zhao.

sentences.zh: 眾既退散，兆因入洛。

translations.literal: The masses having scattered and retreated, Zhao thereby entered Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Once the army had broken and fled, Zhao entered Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 子恭竄于緱氏，仍被執送。

translations.literal: Zigong fled to Gou Shi and was then seized and escorted in custody.
translations.idiomatic: Zigong fled to Gou Shi but was captured and taken away under guard.

sentences.zh: 俄而見釋。

translations.literal: Soon he was released.
translations.idiomatic: He was released shortly afterward.

sentences.zh: 子彪，字文宗。

translations.literal: Zibiao, styled Wenzong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Biao, styled Wenzong.

sentences.zh: 子恭存日，轉授臨潁縣開國侯。

translations.literal: While Zigong was alive, he transferred to him the marquisate of a chief district at Linying.
translations.idiomatic: While Zigong was still alive, he transferred the marquisate of Linying chief district to him.

sentences.zh: 武定末，太子洗馬。

translations.literal: At the end of the Wuding era, he was palace attendant to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Wuding era he served as palace attendant to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 彪弟文瑤，武定中，襲襄城縣開國男。

translations.literal: Biao's younger brother Wenyao—in the Wuding era inherited the barony of a chief district at Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Biao's younger brother Wenyao inherited the barony of Xiangcheng chief district during the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵並降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, both titles were demoted.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi accepted the abdication, both titles were reduced.

sentences.zh: 子恭弟纂，字靈秀。

translations.literal: Zigong's younger brother Zuan, styled Lingxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Zigong's younger brother Zuan, styled Lingxiu.

sentences.zh: 員外散騎侍郎，累遷征虜將軍、通直散騎常侍、涼州大中正，轉太府少卿。

translations.literal: Outside-the-staff Regular Attendant at the Capital Gate; successively promoted to General Who Subdues Barbarians, Regular Attendant at the Direct Gate, Senior Rectifier of Liangzhou, transferred to Vice Director of the Grand Steward's office.
translations.idiomatic: He was outside-the-staff regular attendant at the capital gate, then successively general who subdues barbarians, regular attendant at the direct gate, senior rectifier of Liangzhou, and vice director of the grand steward's office.

sentences.zh: 建義初，遇害河陰，年三十七。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi, he was killed at Heyin, age thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianyi era he was killed at Heyin, at the age of thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈散騎常侍、征北將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously gifted Regular Attendant at the Capital Gate, General Who Campaigns the North, and Governor of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given regular attendant at the capital gate, general who campaigns the north, and governor of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 懷弟奐，字思周，少而謹密。

translations.literal: Huai's younger brother Huan, styled Sizhou, from youth careful and meticulous.
translations.idiomatic: Huai's younger brother Huan, styled Sizhou, was careful and disciplined from youth.

sentences.zh: 初為中書學生。

translations.literal: Initially he was a student at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a student at the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 隨父討敕勒，有斬獲之功，遷中散。

translations.literal: Following his father to suppress the Chile, he had merit in beheading and capture, and was promoted to Central Staff Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He followed his father on campaign against the Chile, won credit in battle, and was promoted to central staff attendant.

sentences.zh: 前後使檢察州鎮十餘所，皆有功績。

translations.literal: Before and after, sent to inspect more than ten prefectures and garrisons, all had achievements.
translations.idiomatic: On more than ten inspection missions to prefectures and garrisons, he achieved results every time.

sentences.zh: 除長樂太守，以母老解官歸養。

translations.literal: Appointed Administrator of Changle; because his mother was old he resigned office to return and support her.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed administrator of Changle, but resigned to go home and care for his aged mother.

sentences.zh: 卒，無子。

translations.literal: He died, without sons.
translations.idiomatic: He died without heirs.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：源賀堂堂，非徒武節而已，其翼戴高宗，庭抑禪讓，殆社稷之臣也。

translations.literal: The historian says: Yuan He was imposing—not merely martial integrity; he supported and attended Emperor Wencheng, restrained in court the abdication ceremony, almost a minister of the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Yuan He was a man of presence—not courage alone. He upheld Emperor Wencheng, checked the disorder of succession in court, and was nearly a pillar of the realm.

sentences.zh: 懷幹略兼舉，出內有聲，繼迹賢考，不墜先業。

translations.literal: Huai combined strategy and talent, had reputation within and without, followed the footsteps of his worthy father, and did not fall from ancestral enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Huai united talent and strategy and won renown at court and beyond, following his worthy father's path without letting the family name decline.

sentences.zh: 子雍効立夏方，身亡冀野，惜乎！

translations.literal: Ziyong established merit in the Xia region, died in the wilds of Ji—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Ziyong won distinction in the Xia region and fell in the wilds of Ji—what a loss!

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 宜其得實 李慈銘云：「『其得』當乙作『得其』。

translations.literal: It is fitting that truth be obtained. Li Ciming states: "『其得』 should be transposed to read 『得其』.
translations.idiomatic: It is fitting that truth be obtained. Li Ciming notes: "qi de should be transposed to read de qi.

sentences.zh: 北史

translations.literal: History of the Northern Dynasties
translations.idiomatic: History of the Northern Dynasties

sentences.zh: 〈卷二八源賀傳〉

translations.literal: 〈Biography of Yuan He, scroll 28〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Biography of Yuan He, scroll 28〉

sentences.zh: 作『宜保其實』，『保』乃『得』字之誤。」

translations.literal: reads 『宜保其實』—『保』 is an error for the character 『得』."
translations.idiomatic: reads yi bao qi shi; bao is a mistaken form of de."

sentences.zh: 顧憶誠言 李慈銘云：「『誠言』本當作『忠言』，此或隋人所追改。

translations.literal: Looking back on sincere words. Li Ciming states: "『誠言』 originally should read 『忠言』; this was perhaps altered by Sui people afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back on sincere words. Li Ciming notes: "cheng yan originally should read zhong yan; this may have been altered by Sui editors.

sentences.zh: 下延伯傳『誠孝』二字亦同。」

translations.literal: Below in Yanbo's biography the two characters 『誠孝』 are the same."
translations.idiomatic: The same applies to the two characters cheng xiao in Yanbo's biography below."

sentences.zh: 西冶都將 諸本「冶」作「治」。

translations.literal: Director of the Western Smelting Office. All editions read "治" for "冶".
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Western Smelting Office. All editions read zhi for ye.

sentences.zh: 按「西治」無義，隋書卷二七百官志中北齊太府寺所統有「諸冶東道」及「諸冶西道」諸局，乃鑄冶機構。

translations.literal: Comment: "Western Governance" makes no sense. In Suishu scroll 27 Bureaucratic Treatise, under the Northern Qi Grand Steward's office there are the bureaus "Various Smelting Offices Eastern Route" and "Various Smelting Offices Western Route"—these are casting and smelting institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Comment: "Western Governance" makes no sense. Suishu, scroll 27, Bureaucratic Treatise, lists under the Northern Qi grand steward's office the bureaus "Various Smelting Offices Eastern Route" and "Various Smelting Offices Western Route"—casting and smelting agencies.

sentences.zh: 北齊多本魏制，「西冶都將」當是管理諸冶西道的官員。

translations.literal: Northern Qi largely followed Wei institutions; "Director of the Western Smelting Office" should be the official managing the Various Smelting Offices Western Route.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi largely followed Wei institutions; "director of the western smelting office" should be the official in charge of the western smelting route.

sentences.zh: 舊本「冶」字帶草，以後各本訛作「治」。

translations.literal: In old editions the character "冶" had the grass radical; later editions corrupted it to "治".
translations.idiomatic: In older editions ye was written with the grass radical; later copies corrupted it to zhi.

sentences.zh: 今改正。

translations.literal: Now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Corrected accordingly.

sentences.zh: 輕恩尚免 北史卷二八源懷傳「輕」作「經」，這裏「輕」字當是形訛。

translations.literal: Light favor still exempts. Beishi scroll 28, Biography of Yuan Huai, reads "經" for "輕"; here "輕" is likely a graphic error.
translations.idiomatic: Light favor still exempts. Beishi, scroll 28, Biography of Yuan Huai, reads jing for qing; qing here is probably a graphic error.

sentences.zh: 臣亡父先臣賀與長孫渴侯陸麗等表迎高宗 北史卷二八「表」作「奉」。

translations.literal: Your subject's deceased father, my late father He, together with Zhangsun Kehou, Lu Li, and others memorialized to welcome Emperor Wencheng. Beishi scroll 28 reads "奉" for "表".
translations.idiomatic: Your subject's deceased father, my late father He, together with Zhangsun Kehou, Lu Li, and others, welcomed Emperor Wencheng. Beishi, scroll 28, reads feng for biao.

sentences.zh: 按上文源賀傳、卷四０陸麗傳都說「奉迎高宗」。

translations.literal: Comment: The Yuan He biography above and scroll 40, Biography of Lu Li, both say "respectfully welcomed Emperor Wencheng."
translations.idiomatic: Comment: The Yuan He biography above and scroll 40, Biography of Lu Li, both say "respectfully welcomed Emperor Wencheng."

sentences.zh: 這裏「表」字當是「奉」之訛。

translations.literal: Here the character "表" should be a corruption of "奉".
translations.idiomatic: Here biao should be a corruption of feng.

sentences.zh: 麗息叡狀秘書 諸本「秘」作「私」，北史卷二八作「秘」。

translations.literal: Li's son Rui submitted a memorial to the Secretariat. All editions read "私" for "秘"; Beishi scroll 28 reads "秘".
translations.idiomatic: Li's son Rui submitted a memorial to the Secretariat. All editions read si for mi; Beishi, scroll 28, reads mi.

sentences.zh: 按「狀私書」不可通。

translations.literal: Comment: "Memorial to the Private Secretariat" is unintelligible.
translations.idiomatic: Comment: "memorial to the private secretariat" makes no sense.

sentences.zh: 秘書省掌修史，藏有文書檔案，當是陸叡上狀秘書省，請查核其父所謂「功績」。

translations.literal: The Secretariat oversaw compilation of history and kept documentary archives; this should mean Lu Rui submitted a memorial to the Secretariat requesting verification of his father's alleged "meritorious deeds."
translations.idiomatic: The secretariat oversaw historiography and kept the archives; Lu Rui must have submitted a memorial to the secretariat asking it to verify his father's claimed "merits."

sentences.zh: 這次源懷上表論「功」，下文詔書也說「訪之史官，頗亦言此」。

translations.literal: On this occasion Yuan Huai submitted a memorial discussing "merit"; the edict below also says "Inquiring of the historiographers, they too largely say this."
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion Yuan Huai memorialized on "merit," and the edict below likewise says, "When the historiographers were consulted, they too largely confirmed it."

sentences.zh: 可知這類前朝臣僚事跡例由秘書所屬史官查核。

translations.literal: From this one can know that deeds of former court officials were routinely verified by historiographers subordinate to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that the deeds of former officials were routinely checked by the historiographers under the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 「私」乃「秘」字形訛，今據改。

translations.literal: "私" is a graphic corruption of "秘"; emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Si is a graphic corruption of mi; emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 麗以父功而獲河山之賞 按「麗」乃「叡」之誤，觀上文自見。

translations.literal: Li received the reward of rivers and mountains for his father's merit. Comment: "Li" is an error for "Rui"; this is clear from the text above.
translations.idiomatic: Li received the reward of rivers and mountains for his father's merit. Comment: Li is an error for Rui, as the passage above makes clear.

sentences.zh: 可依比授馮翊郡開國公邑百戶 北史卷二八「百」上有「九」字。

translations.literal: May be granted by parallel precedent the Duke of Fengyi Chief District with fief of one hundred households. Beishi scroll 28 has the character "九" before "百".
translations.idiomatic: May be granted by parallel precedent the duke of Fengyi chief district with a fief of one hundred households. Beishi, scroll 28, has jiu before bai.

sentences.zh: 按公的封戶百戶太少，當脫「九」字。

translations.literal: Comment: one hundred feudal households for a duke is too few; the character "九" must be missing.
translations.idiomatic: Comment: a fief of one hundred households is too small for a duke; jiu must have dropped out.

sentences.zh: 子紹襲景明初詔復王爵 張森楷云：「按懷以正始三年卒，再傳而至紹，不得在景明初也。」

translations.literal: Zishao inherited the edict restoring princely rank in the early Jingming era. Zhang Senkai states: "Comment: Huai died in the third year of Zhengshi; passing through two more generations to Shao, it cannot be in the early Jingming era.
