translations.idiomatic: Zishao inherited the edict restoring princely rank in the early Jingming era. Zhang Senkai notes: "Comment: Huai died in the third year of Zhengshi; two generations later, Shao could not have inherited in the early Jingming era.

sentences.zh: 按「景明」年號在「正始」前，哪有源懷未死，爵已傳襲到曾孫之理。

translations.literal: 」 Comment: the Jingming reign title comes before Zhengshi—how could Yuan Huai not yet be dead while the title had already passed through inheritance to a great-grandson?
translations.idiomatic: The Jingming reign precedes Zhengshi—how could the title have passed to a great-grandson while Yuan Huai was still alive?

sentences.zh: 據卷一０孝莊紀建義元年四月稱：「馮翊郡開國公源紹景復先爵隴西王。」

translations.literal: According to scroll 10, Annals of Emperor Xiaozhuang, fourth month of the first year of Jianyi: "Yuan Shao Jing of Fengyi Chief District restored the former title of Prince of Longxi."
translations.idiomatic: According to scroll 10, Annals of Emperor Xiaozhuang, fourth month of the first year of Jianyi: "Yuan Shao Jing, duke of Fengyi chief district, restored the former title of prince of Longxi."

sentences.zh: 「紹景」即「紹」，傳雙名單稱。

translations.literal: " "Shaojing" means "Shao"; the biography uses the double name in abbreviated form.
translations.idiomatic: Shaojing" means Shao—the biography abbreviates his double name.

sentences.zh: 這裏「景明」二字顯誤。

translations.literal: Here the two characters "Jingming" are clearly in error.
translations.idiomatic: The reference to the Jingming era here is clearly mistaken.

sentences.zh: 苟逼同行 諸本「同」訛「固」，今據冊府卷四二八

translations.literal: If forced to travel together. All editions corrupt "together" as "firm"; now emended according to Cefu, scroll 428
translations.idiomatic: If forced to travel together: all editions misread tong (together) as gu (firm); emended according to Cefu, scroll 428

sentences.zh: 〈五０九九頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 5099〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈page 5099〉

sentences.zh: 改。

translations.literal: —emended.
translations.idiomatic: —emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 假蕭衍昏狂 諸本「昏」訛「皆」，今據冊府卷四七二

translations.literal: Even if Xiao Yan were muddled and mad. All editions corrupt "muddled" as "all"; now emended according to Cefu, scroll 472
translations.idiomatic: Even if Xiao Yan were muddled and mad: all editions misread hun (muddled) as jie (all); emended according to Cefu, scroll 472

sentences.zh: 〈五六三四頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 5634〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈page 5634〉

sentences.zh: 改。

translations.literal: —emended.
translations.idiomatic: —emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 河州羌却鐵怱反 諸本「怱」作「忽」，北史卷二八源子恭傳作「怱」。

translations.literal: The Qiang of Hezhou, Que Tiecong, rebelled. All editions read "cong" as "hu"; Beishi, scroll 28, Biography of Yuan Zigong, reads "cong".
translations.idiomatic: The Hezhou Qiang leader Que Tiecong rebelled. Most editions read cong as hu; the History of the Northern Dynasties, scroll 28, Biography of Yuan Zigong, has cong.

sentences.zh: 按卷九肅宗紀神龜元年七月、卷四二寇讚附寇治傳都作「怱」。

translations.literal: According to scroll 9, Annals of Emperor Suzong, seventh month of the first year of Shengui, and scroll 42, Biography of Kou Zan with appended Biography of Kou Zhi, all read "cong".
translations.idiomatic: Scroll 9 (Annals of Emperor Suzong, Shengui 1.7) and scroll 42 (Biography of Kou Zan, with Kou Zhi appended) all have cong.

sentences.zh: 「忽」字訛，今據改。

translations.literal: The character "hu" is erroneous; emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Hu is a corruption; emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 參卷二七校記[六]。

translations.literal: See collation note [6] to scroll 27.
translations.idiomatic: See collation note 6 to scroll 27.

sentences.zh: 侍中領軍臣叉總動作官 諸本「總」作「物」，冊府卷五八三

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary and Commander of the Guard Chen Cha supervised the work officers. All editions read "supervise" as "object"; Cefu, scroll 583
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-ordinary and commander of the guard Chen Cha supervised the work officers. All editions read zong (supervise) as wu (object); Cefu, scroll 583

sentences.zh: 〈六九八二頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 6982〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈page 6982〉

sentences.zh: 作「總勤」。

translations.literal: reads "supervise diligently".
translations.idiomatic: reads zong qin (supervise diligently).

sentences.zh: 李慈銘云：「『物』當是『總』字之誤。

translations.literal: Li Ciming said: "'Object' must be an error for 'supervise.'
translations.idiomatic: Li Ciming said, "Wu must be an error for zong (supervise).

sentences.zh: 因隸俗書『總』作『惣』，遂誤作『物』。」

translations.literal: Because in clerical and vulgar script 'supervise' was written 'zong,' it was then mistaken as 'object.'"
translations.idiomatic: In clerical and vulgar script zong was written as a variant form, which was then misread as wu."

sentences.zh: 按「總動」「總勤」不知孰是，「物」字據冊府及李說改作「總」。

translations.literal: Comment: whether "supervise work" or "supervise diligently" is correct is uncertain; the character "object" is changed to "supervise" on the authority of Cefu and Li's explanation.
translations.idiomatic: Whether zong dong or zong qin is correct is uncertain; wu is emended to zong on the authority of Cefu and Li Ciming.

sentences.zh: 以子恭為當郡別將 百衲本、汲本「當」字下空一格，南、北、殿、局四本「當」下注「闕」字。

translations.literal: Zigong was made acting separate commander of the commandery. In the patchwork and Ji editions there is a blank space below "acting"; in the Southern, Northern, Palace, and Bureau editions a note "missing" is placed below "acting."
translations.idiomatic: Zigong was made acting separate commander of the commandery. The patchwork and Ji editions leave a blank after dang (acting); four other editions mark que (missing) there.

sentences.zh: 按「當郡別將」可通，似無脫文，今不空格，刪「闕」字。

translations.literal: Comment: "acting commander of the commandery" makes sense and seems not to lack text; no blank is left and the note "missing" is deleted.
translations.idiomatic: Dang jun bie jiang (acting separate commander of the commandery) makes sense; no blank is inserted and the que (missing) note is removed.

sentences.zh: 元象元年 李慈銘、張森楷並云此句下當脫「卒」字。

translations.literal: First year of Yuanxiang. Li Ciming and Zhang Senkai both say that below this sentence the character "died" has dropped out.
translations.idiomatic: First year of Yuanxiang. Li Ciming and Zhang Senkai both hold that the word zu (died) has dropped out after this line.
